https://testlify.com/knowledge-base/ente.description: This white paper offers a comprehensive guide to building a modern hiring stack for enterprises. From ATS to analytics, learn how to optimize each layer of your recruitment infrastructure.

https://testlify.com/knowledge-base/hiri.description: This white paper uncovers why your hiring funnel is losing top talent. Learn how to identify gaps and implement strategies that boost hiring efficiency.

https://testlify.com/knowledge-base/skil.description: Learn practical steps to shift from resumes to real capabilities. This white paper explores how skills-based hiring helps organizations attract top talent, reduce bias, and future-proof their workforce.

https://testlify.com/knowledge-base/buye.description: Discover how to choose the right AI assessment platform with expert insights, feature comparisons, and practical evaluation tips.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: An Employer of Record (usually just called an EOR) is a third-party company that legally employs workers on your behalf in countries where you don’t have your own entity. What is an Employer of record (EOR)? Picture this. You have found the perfect senior developer in Portugal. She’s ready to start next month. But your…

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/zero-ba.title: Zero Based Budgeting
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/zero-ba.description: Zero-based budgeting (ZBB) is a budgeting method in which all expenses must be justified for each new budget period, regardless of whether they were incurred in the prior budget period.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/yellow-.title: Yellow Dog Contract
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/yellow-.description: A yellow-dog contract is an agreement between an employer and an employee that prohibits the employee from joining or being a member of a labor union while employed by the company.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/xml-and.title: XML and HR-XML (Extensive Markup language)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/xml-and.description: XML is a markup language that provides a standardized format for structuring and storing data. HR-XML is a standardized data definition and guidelines for representing human resources information in XML.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/wrongfu.title: Wrongful dismissal/ wrongful termination
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/wrongfu.description: Wrongful dismissal is a legal term used to describe a situation where an employee is terminated from their job in a manner that breaches the terms of their employment contract.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/worldat.title: WorldatWork
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/worldat.description: WorldatWork is a global non-profit organization that provides education, certification, research, and advocacy in the field of compensation and total rewards.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workwee.title: Workweek
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workwee.description: A workweek is a regularly recurring period of seven consecutive 24-hour periods designated in advance by an employer as the basis for computing regular pay and overtime pay for employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/positio.title: Position
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/positio.description: A position in HR refers to a specific job or role within an organization, with its own set of duties, responsibilities, and requirements.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/market-.title: Market Pricing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/market-.description: Market Pricing is a HR technique to determine job value and set fair, data-driven compensation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/johari-.title: Johari window
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/johari-.description: The Johari Window is a model used to improve self-awareness and relationship awareness through communication and self-discovery by dividing self-knowledge into four categories: open, hidden, blind, and unknown.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-sha.title: Job Sharing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-sha.description: Job sharing is a flexible work arrangement where two employees split responsibilities and duties of a full-time job by working part-time schedules that overlap.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hosted-.title: Hosted Delivery Model
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hosted-.description: A hosted delivery model for HR software provides internet-based access, cost savings, scalability, and automatic updates from a third-party provider.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/host-co.title: Host-country nationals (HCNs)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/host-co.description: Host-country nationals (HCNs) are individuals who are citizens or permanent residents of the country where an organization operates and works, serving as locally hired employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/host-co.title: Host-country
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/host-co.description: The host-country is where an organization operates and its HR policies and laws differ from home-country for international assignments.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.title: Workplace Relationships
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.description: Workplace relationships refer to the connections and interactions between individuals in a professional setting.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.title: Workplace Phobia
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.description: Workplace phobia, also known as work-related social phobia or occupational phobia, is a type of anxiety disorder characterized by intense fear and avoidance of work-related situations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/deforma.title: Déformation Professionnelle
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/deforma.description: Déformation professionnelle refers to the way a job shapes a person’s behavior and thinking, often resulting in both positive and negative effects on work and personal life.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.title: Workplace Health Surveillance
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.description: Workplace health surveillance is the systematic monitoring of the health of workers who are exposed to specific health risks as a result of their work.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.title: Workplace Gossip
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.description: Workplace gossip is the sharing of personal, unverified, and often negative information about coworkers, managers, or the organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/trainin.title: Training And Development
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/trainin.description: Training and Development refer to the process of acquiring knowledge, skills, and abilities in order to perform a task or job more effectively.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/trainin.title: Training Needs Analysis
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/trainin.description: Training Needs Analysis is the process of identifying the gap between an organization’s current and desired performance, and determining the training and development needs of employees to close that gap.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/trainin.title: Training
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/trainin.description: Training is the process of acquiring knowledge, skills, and abilities in order to perform a task or job more effectively.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/traditi.title: Traditional Authority
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/traditi.description: Traditional Authority is a form of governance that is based on customary laws, traditions, and cultural practices that have been passed down through generations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.title: Workplace Flexibility
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.description: Workplace flexibility refers to the ability for employees to have control over when, where, and how they work, allowing for a better work-life balance and improved job satisfaction.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.title: Workplace Deviance
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.description: Workplace deviance refers to behaviors that break organizational norms. This includes theft, harassment, unethical practices, and more.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.title: Workplace Democracy
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.description: Workplace democracy is a management style where employees have a say in decision-making and running of a company, leading to a democratic and participatory work environment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.title: What Is Workplace Bullying?
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workpla.description: Workplace bullying is repeated behavior that undermines employees. Learn types, legal status, investigation steps, and enterprise HR prevention policies.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/working.title: Working Capital Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/working.description: Working capital management is the process of efficiently managing a company’s short-term assets and liabilities to balance liquidity and investment in growth, with the goal of financial stability.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workfor.title: Workforce Readiness
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workfor.description: Workforce readiness refers to the skills, knowledge, and attributes required for success in the workplace. It impacts both individual and organizational success by promoting productivity, competitiveness, and job satisfaction.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workfor.title: Workforce Management Software
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workfor.description: Workforce management software is a tool that helps organizations manage and optimize their workforce, improving productivity, efficiency, and profitability through scheduling, staffing, time tracking, performance management, and budgeting.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workfor.title: Workforce Management (WFM)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workfor.description: WFM optimizes workforce scheduling, compliance, and performance for enterprise HR teams. Reduce labor costs and improve operational efficiency at scale.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workfor.title: Workforce
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workfor.description: The workforce encompasses all employees of a company, impacting its productivity, competitiveness, and success.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/video-i.title: Video Interview
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/video-i.description: Video interview is a method of conducting job interviews remotely using video conferencing technology.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/vertica.title: Vertical Organization
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/vertica.description: A Vertical Organization is a type of organizational structure characterized by a clear chain of command and defined roles, with a hierarchical structure, where decision-making is centralized at the top.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/variabl.title: Variable Pay
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/variabl.description: Variable pay is a type of compensation that can fluctuate based on performance and is used to align employee performance with company goals.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/vaping/.title: Vaping
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/vaping/.description: Vaping refers to the use of electronic cigarettes or other vaping devices, and it is subject to laws and regulations regarding smoking.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/values-.title: Values Statement
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/values-.description: A values statement is a document that defines and communicates a company’s core values and beliefs, intended to guide behavior and decision-making.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/vacancy.title: Vacancy Rate
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/vacancy.description: The vacancy rate is a metric that measures the percentage of open positions in a company that has not been filled.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/utiliza.title: Utilization Analysis
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/utiliza.description: Utilization analysis evaluates the efficient use of resources to optimize resource allocation and increase efficiency and productivity in an organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/upskill.title: Upskilling
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/upskill.description: Upskilling is enhancing skills to improve job performance and increase earning potential, leading to career advancement and a more competitive organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/up-or-o.title: Up or Out
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/up-or-o.description: Up or Out is an HR approach that requires employees to continually improve and advance in their careers, with the expectation that they will be promoted or leave the company.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/untappe.title: Untapped Talent
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/untappe.description: Untapped talent refers to potential skills or abilities within employees that are yet to be fully utilized or developed by an organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/unrepor.title: Unreported Employment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/unrepor.description: Unreported Employment refers to employment that is not reported to the government or is hidden from official records.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/union/.title: Union
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/union/.description: A union is an organization of workers that protects and promotes the rights and interests of its members through collective bargaining with their employer.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/unfair-.title: Unfair Selection
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/unfair-.description: Unfair selection refers to discriminatory HR practices in hiring, leading to unequal job opportunities and potential legal consequences.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workers.title: Workers’ Compensation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/workers.description: Workers’ compensation is a system of insurance that provides financial support and protection to employees who are injured or become ill as a result of their work.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/work-li.title: Work Life Employee Benefits
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/work-li.description: Work-life Employee Benefits are a set of perks offered by employers to help their employees achieve a better balance between their work and personal lives.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/work-li.title: Work-life Balance
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/work-li.description: Work-life Balance is the concept of balancing time and energy between work and personal pursuits, to achieve overall well-being.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/work-st.title: Work Stoppage
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/work-st.description: Work Stoppage refers to a temporary halt in the operation of a business or industry caused by a strike, lockout, or labor dispute, which can lead to loss of productivity, revenue, reputation and job loss.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/white-c.title: What Is a White Collar Worker?
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/white-c.description: A white collar worker performs knowledge-based office work. Learn types, examples, FLSA rules, and how enterprise HR teams assess white collar candidates.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/whistle.title: What is a Whistleblower?
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/whistle.description: A whistleblower reports illegal or unethical workplace conduct. Learn HR definitions, SOX & Dodd-Frank protections, and how to build an enterprise policy.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/total-r.title: Total Rewards
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/total-r.description: Total rewards refer to the comprehensive compensation package offered by an employer to its employees. It is a holistic approach to employee compensation that goes beyond traditional salary and benefits.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/unfair-.title: What Is Unfair Labor Practice?
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/unfair-.description: An unfair labor practice (ULP) violates NLRA Section 8. Learn employer and union prohibitions, NLRB charge process, and enterprise prevention strategies.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/unfair-.title: Unfair Dismissal
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/unfair-.description: Unfair dismissal is termination without a valid reason or proper procedure can be various types like automatic, conduct, redundancy, discrimination, whistle-blowing, or retaliation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/wellnes.title: Wellness Program
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/wellnes.description: A Wellness Program is an organized approach to promoting health and well-being in the workplace, typically including health screenings, education, exercise programs, stress management, nutrition, and other resources.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/wellbei.title: Wellbeing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/wellbei.description: Wellbeing is a holistic concept that encompasses physical, mental, emotional, and social well-being, it is an overall sense of contentment and satisfaction with life.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/weingar.title: What Are Weingarten Rights?
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/weingar.description: Learn what Weingarten Rights are, when they apply, and what enterprise HR teams must do when an employee invokes them under NLRA Section 7.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/total-r.title: Total Remuneration
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/total-r.description: A total remuneration is a comprehensive approach to compensation and benefits, looking at how employees are rewarded for their work, including wages, benefits, bonuses, and forms of payment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/wage-dr.title: Wage Drift
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/wage-dr.description: Wage Drift refers to the gradual increase in wages over time due to inflation and other factors, rather than formal negotiations or agreements.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/unexpec.title: Unexpected time off (unplanned leave)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/unexpec.description: Unexpected time off is unplanned absence from work, usually due to personal reasons, which can disrupt employer’s operations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/total-q.title: Total Quality Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/total-q.description: TQM is a long-term approach to management that can help organizations improve efficiency, reduce costs, and increase customer satisfaction.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/w-4/.title: W-4
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/w-4/.description: W-4 form is used by employees to indicate their tax withholding status to their employer, by providing information such as their filing status and number of dependents, which the employer uses to determine how much money to withhold from the employee’s paycheck for federal income taxes.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/unemplo.title: Unemployed
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/unemplo.description: Not working, actively seeking employment, not included in the labor force, part of the unemployed population.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/total-c.title: Total Compensation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/total-c.description: Total compensation refers to the total monetary value of all the benefits and remuneration employees receive in exchange for their work. It includes both direct and indirect forms of compensation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/w-2/.title: W-2
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/w-2/.description: W-2 forms are official documentation of an employee’s wages and taxes withheld, used for accurate tax reporting and simplifying the tax filing process, but can be costly, time-consuming, and vulnerable to identity theft.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/underwr.title: Underwriter
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/underwr.description: An underwriter is a professional who assesses risk, makes decisions on coverage, loan or bond, and sets terms and conditions, determining premium or interest rate.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/title-v.title: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/title-v.description: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 is a federal law prohibiting workplace discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/volunte.title: Volunteerism
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/volunte.description: Volunteerism is the act of working for the benefit of others without receiving compensation, it helps to address social needs, improve quality of life, and increase civic engagement.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/time-to.title: Time to Fill
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/time-to.description: Time to fill is a metric that measures the time it takes to fill a job opening, from the job posted to a new employee starting work.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/unconsc.title: Unconscious Bias
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/unconsc.description: Unconscious bias refers to attitudes or stereotypes that unconsciously affect perceptions, decisions, and actions leading to discrimination and inequality in the workplace.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/volunta.title: Voluntary Redundancy
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/volunta.description: Voluntary Redundancy is a program offered by some employers where employees can choose to leave their jobs and receive a financial payout in exchange for not seeking employment or legal action against the company.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/two-fac.title: Two-factor theory
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/two-fac.description: The Two-factor theory explains how certain factors in the work environment can affect a person’s motivation and job satisfaction; it’s composed of hygiene factors and motivators.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/time-to.title: Time to Hire
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/time-to.description: Time to hire is a metric that measures the amount of time it takes for a company to fill a job opening, from the date the job is posted to the date an offer is accepted.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/volunta.title: Voluntary Reduced Worktime
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/volunta.description: Voluntary Reduced Worktime (VRWT) offers employees the opportunity to work fewer hours for better work-life balance, but may come with reduced pay and benefits.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/volunta.title: Voluntary Benefit
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/volunta.description: Voluntary Benefits give employees the ability to choose additional coverage that aligns with their unique needs and preferences, leading to increased employee satisfaction and retention.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/turnove.title: Turnover Rate
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/turnove.description: Turnover rate is the rate at which employees leave a company, typically calculated as a percentage of the total number of employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/time-an.title: Time and Attendance software
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/time-an.description: Time and attendance software are computer programs that track and manage employee time and attendance data.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/vision-.title: Vision Statement
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/vision-.description: A clear, inspiring statement that guides an organization’s decision-making and goals, aligns efforts, communicates values, and serves as a foundation for long-term success.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/time-an.title: Time and a Half
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/time-an.description: Time-and-a-half refers to paying employees one and a half times their regular pay rate for any hours worked beyond their standard workweek.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/virtual.title: Virtual HR
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/virtual.description: Virtual HR refers to the use of technology to manage Human Resources (HR) tasks and processes.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/turnove.title: Turnover Costs
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/turnove.description: Turnover costs refer to the expenses associated with replacing departing employees, such as recruitment, training, and lost productivity.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/viral-m.title: Viral Marketing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/viral-m.description: Viral Marketing is a low-cost strategy that relies on social networks and word-of-mouth to spread a message, aiming to increase brand awareness and sales.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/third-p.title: What Is Third-Party Harassment?
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/third-p.description: Third-party harassment occurs when vendors, clients, or contractors harass employees. Learn employer liability, EEOC rules, and enterprise prevention policy.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/turnove.title: Turnover
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/turnove.description: Turnover is the rate at which employees leave a company and need to be replaced. High turnover can negatively impact a company’s productivity, morale, and reputation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/summary.title: Summary of Material Modifications (SMM)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/summary.description: Summary of Material Modifications (SMM) is a document that summarizes changes made to employee benefit plans, explains the significance of changes and ensures compliance with regulations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/third-c.title: Third-country Nationals (TCNs)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/third-c.description: Third-country nationals (TCNs) are individuals who are neither citizens of the country where they are currently residing nor citizens of the country where they intend to work.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/summary.title: Summary Dismissal
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/summary.description: Summary Dismissal is the immediate termination of an employee’s contract without notice or pay due to serious misconduct such as gross insubordination or theft. It’s considered a last resort and should be done fairly and legally.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/third-p.title: Third Party Administrator (TPA)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/third-p.description: A Third-Party Administrator (TPA) is a company that provides administrative services to other companies, typically in employee benefits and insurance claims.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/theory-.title: Theory X and Theory Y
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/theory-.description: Theory X and Theory Y are management theories developed by Douglas McGregor in the 1960s as part of his study of human behavior in the workplace.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/success.title: Succession Planning
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/success.description: Succession Planning is a process of identifying, developing & implementing strategies to attract, retain & develop potential leaders to fill key positions within an organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/the-big.title: The Big Three
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/the-big.description: The “Big Three” refers to the largest credit reporting agencies (CRAs) in the United States: Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/subscri.title: Subscription Solutions
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/subscri.description: Subscription Solutions offer flexible, cost-effective access to a wide range of services and products, but can also lead to dependency and ongoing costs, and limited control over the service.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/transit.title: Transitional Employment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/transit.description: Transitional employment refers to temporary jobs provided to individuals to help them transition back into the workforce.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/tempora.title: What Is a Temporary Employee?
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/tempora.description: Temporary employees fill short-term needs without permanent headcount. Learn types, co-employment risks, and FLSA rules for enterprise HR teams.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/structu.title: Structured Interview
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/structu.description: Structured Interview is a type of job interview in which a set of pre-determined questions are asked to all candidates in a consistent manner and to rate the candidate’s responses on a standardized scale, in order to ensure fairness and objectivity.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/strikeb.title: Strikebreaker: definition, legal framework and HR guide
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/strikeb.description: Strikebreaker is a person hired by employer to replace striking employees during a labor strike, with goal of keeping operations running, breaking solidarity of striking workers, maintaining productivity and avoiding lost revenue.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/transge.title: Transgender in the workplace: HR guide and legal overview
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/transge.description: Transgender refers to individuals whose gender identity does not match the sex assigned to them at birth. They may take steps to transition to the gender with which they identify.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/telecom.title: Telecommuting: definition, policy and HR guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/telecom.description: Telecommuting, also known as remote work or telework, is an arrangement in which employees perform their job duties outside the office, typically from their homes.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/stress-.title: What Is a Stress Interview?
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/stress-.description: A stress interview deliberately creates pressure to test how candidates respond under duress. Learn types, questions, legal risks, and HR best practices.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/team-bu.title: Team building
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/team-bu.description: Team building is creating a robust and cohesive team that can work well together even with a common goal or objective.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/transfo.title: Transformational Leadership
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/transfo.description: Transformational leadership is a leadership style that inspires and motivates followers to become better versions of themselves and achieve their goals.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/strateg.title: Strategic Planning
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/strateg.description: Strategic Planning is the process of developing a long-term direction and performance plan for an organization, through goals setting, resource allocation and continual improvement.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/tacit-k.title: Tacit knowledge: definition, examples and HR guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/tacit-k.description: Tacit knowledge refers to knowledge that is difficult to express or transfer through communication.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/taxable.title: Taxable Income
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/taxable.description: Taxable income is the total amount of money or compensation an individual or organization earns in a given tax year that is subject to income tax.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/strateg.title: Strategic HRM
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/strateg.description: Strategic Human Resource Management is the process of aligning the HR function with the strategic objectives of an organization, to improve performance and competitiveness.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/t-shape.title: T-shaped skills: definition, examples and HR guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/t-shape.description: T-shaped skills are a combination of deep expertise in a specific field and a broad range of skills in related fields.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/system-.title: System of Record
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/system-.description: A System of Record (SOR) is a system used to store and manage official, authoritative data for an organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/tax-ide.title: Tax Identification Number (TIN)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/tax-ide.description: A Tax Identification Number (TIN) is a unique number assigned by a country’s tax authorities to individuals and organizations to identify and track tax liability.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/system-.title: System Discrimination
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/system-.description: Systemic discrimination refers to patterns of discrimination built into systems, policies, and practices of an organization or society, often subtle and difficult to identify.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/tax/.title: Tax
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/tax/.description: Tax is a financial charge imposed by a government on individuals, businesses, and other entities to fund various public services and programs.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/system-.title: System Changeover
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/system-.description: System changeover is the process of transitioning a system from one state or configuration to another to minimize downtime and disruptions while ensuring the new configuration is functional.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/targete.title: Targeted Selection
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/targete.description: Targeted selection is a process used in recruitment that involves identifying specific characteristics, qualifications, and skills for a particular job and then using these criteria to evaluate and select candidates.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/tangibl.title: Tangible rewards
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/tangibl.description: Tangible rewards are physical items or experiences offered as recognition or incentive for achieving a specific goal or performance level. These rewards include cash bonuses, gift cards, merchandise, travel, etc.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/talent-.title: Talent pooling
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/talent-.description: Talent pooling is a recruitment strategy that focuses on identifying, attracting, and retaining a pool of potential candidates for future job openings within an organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/suspens.title: Suspension
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/suspens.description: Suspension is the temporary cessation or removal of an action, privilege, or activity, often used as a disciplinary measure.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/supply-.title: Supply Chain Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/supply-.description: Supply chain management coordinates and manages the production and delivery of goods and services.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/talent-.title: What is talent management software?
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/talent-.description: Talent management software is a category of HR technology that centralizes talent acquisition, onboarding, learning and development, performance management, and succession planning in one platform. https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/supplie.title: Supplier Diversity
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/supplie.description: Supplier diversity is the practice of actively seeking out and working with diverse suppliers to promote equal opportunities, cost savings, innovation and economic growth.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/supplem.title: Supplemental Unemployment Benefits (SUB)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/supplem.description: Supplemental Unemployment Benefits (SUB) duration depends on the employer’s plan; it may be for a specific time or until the employee returns to work.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/talent-.title: What is talent management?
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/talent-.description: Talent management is the process of identifying, developing, and retaining employees who have the potential to become future leaders or key contributors to an organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/talent-.title: What is talent acquisition?
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/talent-.description: Talent acquisition is identifying, attracting, assessing, and hiring the best-suited candidates for a company’s open positions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/stop-lo.title: What is stop-loss insurance?
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/stop-lo.description: Stop-Loss Insurance is a type of insurance that limits the financial risk of large claims or catastrophic losses for self-insured businesses, by setting a coverage limit, or “stop-loss” point, beyond which the insurer will pay for claims.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/stay-in.title: Stay interview
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/stay-in.description: Stay Interviews are conducted with current employees to understand why they stay with the organization, and what factors contribute to their job satisfaction and engagement, used to retain valuable employees and improve overall employee satisfaction.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/statuto.title: Statutory employee
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/statuto.description: Statutory Employee is an individual who is considered an employee for tax purposes but not for other legal or regulatory purposes, typically used for independent contractors to provide tax benefits, clarify status, simplify tax process, align with labor laws, and reduce costs.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/statute.title: Statute of limitations in employment law
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/statute.description: Statute of Limitations is a law that sets a time limit within which legal action can be taken for a particular type of crime or civil case, ensuring fairness to the accused, prompt reporting, repose, preservation of evidence, and balancing the rights of both parties.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/staffin.title: What is staffing in HR?
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/staffin.description: Staffing is the process of recruiting, hiring, and managing employees in an organization, to ensure that the organization has the right number and type of employees with the necessary skills and qualifications to meet its business objectives.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/spot-aw.title: Spot Award
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/spot-aw.description: Spot Awards are a form of recognition and incentive given to employees for exceptional performance, typically given on the spot in cash or non-cash form, to motivate and inspire continued high performance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/supervi.title: Supervisor
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/supervi.description: A supervisor is a management position responsible for overseeing and guiding the work of a team of employees, implementing policies and procedures, and ensuring goals and objectives are met.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/superio.title: Superior-subordinate Communication
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/superio.description: Superior-subordinate communication is important for effective guidance, trust building, alignment with company culture, fostering a positive work environment, and employee engagement and satisfaction.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/summary.title: Summary Plan Description (SPD)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/summary.description: A Summary Plan Description (SPD) is a document that provides a summary of the major features and provisions of an employee benefit plan.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/society.title: Society of Human Resource Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/society.description: Society of Human Resource Management is a professional organization for HR professionals, promoting the value of HR and providing resources and networking opportunities.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.title: Social Recruitment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.description: Social recruitment is the use of social media platforms to attract, identify, and engage job candidates, allowing companies to reach a larger and more diverse pool of talent.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.title: Social Networking
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.description: Social networking refers to using online platforms to build and maintain relationships, share information and connect with others, typically through social media sites like Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.title: Social Media Background Screening
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.description: Social media background screening allows employers to obtain additional information about job candidates and make more informed hiring decisions by verifying qualifications, conduct, and any red flags.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.title: Social Media
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.description: Social media refers to online platforms where users can create and share content or participate in social networking.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.title: Social Marketing Workflows
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.description: Social Marketing workflow refers to the series of steps and tasks to execute social media strategy in the HR context, such as creating content, scheduling, engagement, tracking analytics, and adjusting strategy while ensuring compliance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sphr-se.title: SPHR (Senior professional in Human Resources)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sphr-se.description: SPHR (Senior Professional in Human Resources) is a professional certification offered by the Human Resource Certification Institute (HRCI) for experienced human resource professionals, recognize them as experts in the field of human resources and valuable assets to their organizations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.title: Social HR
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.description: Social HR uses digital platforms and social media to support human resources activities such as recruitment, employee engagement, and employer branding.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/span-of.title: Span of Control
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/span-of.description: Span of Control refers to the number of subordinates that a manager or supervisor is responsible for managing and directing; it can be narrow or wide.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.title: Social Currency
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.description: Social currency refers to the value gained from social connections and relationships in the workplace, impacting employee engagement and job satisfaction.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sourcin.title: Sourcing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sourcin.description: Sourcing refers to the process of identifying and acquiring goods, services, and raw materials that are needed for the production of a product or the delivery of a service.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/softwar.title: Software As A Service (SaaS)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/softwar.description: Software As A Service (SaaS) is a delivery model in which a third-party provider hosts software and makes it available to customers over the internet, on a subscription basis.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/soft-sk.title: Soft Skills
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/soft-sk.description: Soft Skills are personal attributes and characteristics that enable individuals to interact effectively and harmoniously with others, such as communication, teamwork, problem solving, time management, and leadership.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.title: Social Collaboration
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/social-.description: Social collaboration refers to the use of digital tools to communicate, share information and work together towards a common goal.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/skill-b.title: Skill Based Pay
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/skill-b.description: Skill-based pay is a system of compensation where employees are paid based on their level of skill and competency in a specific area or job.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/skill/.title: Skill
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/skill/.description: Ability to perform a task or activity acquired through experience, training, or education.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/six-sig.title: Six Sigma
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/six-sig.description: Six Sigma is a methodology for process improvement that aims for near-perfection by reducing defects and variability through data analysis and statistical tools.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/situati.title: Situational leadership
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/situati.description: Situational Leadership is a leadership theory that proposes leaders should adapt their leadership style to the development level of the individual or group they are leading.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/shrm-so.title: SHRM (Society for Human Resource Management)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/shrm-so.description: SHRM (Society for Human Resource Management) is a professional organization for human resource management professionals, providing education, resources, and networking opportunities.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/short-t.title: Short-term disability
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/short-t.description: Short-term disability is a benefit that pays employees during temporary disabilities, usually several weeks to a few months.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/shift-w.title: Shift Work Sleep Disorder (SWSD)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/shift-w.description: Shift Work Sleep Disorder (SWSD) is a condition caused by disruption of circadian rhythm due to non-traditional work schedules, resulting in insomnia, excessive sleepiness, fatigue, irritability, and other symptoms.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/shift-m.title: Shift Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/shift-m.description: Shift management is the process of organizing and coordinating employee schedules to ensure proper staffing and efficient operations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sexual-.title: Sexual Orientation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sexual-.description: Sexual orientation is an individual’s attraction to others, important for respect and support in workplace diversity.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sexual-.title: Sexual Harassment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sexual-.description: Sexual harassment is any unwanted or unwelcome sexual behavior that creates a hostile or offensive work environment; it’s a form of discrimination that is illegal under federal and state laws.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sex-dis.title: Sex Discrimination
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sex-dis.description: Sex discrimination is treating someone differently based on their gender or sex, in ways such as hiring, pay, or harassment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/severan.title: Severance
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/severan.description: Severance is financial assistance for employees after termination due to layoffs or business closures.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/seven-d.title: Seven Deadly Diseases of Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/seven-d.description: The Seven Deadly Diseases of Management are common mistakes in management that can negatively impact an organization, they are Arrogance, Incompetence, Intolerance, Lassitude, Pessimism, Avarice, and Procrastination.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/serious.title: Serious Health Condition
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/serious.description: Serious Health Condition is a condition requiring an extended leave, defined under the FMLA as inpatient care or treatment by a healthcare provider.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sensiti.title: Sensitivity Training
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sensiti.description: Sensitivity training is a type of training that aims to increase awareness and understanding of different cultures, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities, and other diverse groups.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/senior-.title: Senior Professional in Human Resources (SPHR)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/senior-.description: The Senior Professional in Human Resources (SPHR) certification is a professional certification for individuals who demonstrate knowledge and expertise in the field of human resources management.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/self-se.title: Self-service HR
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/self-se.description: Self-service HR allows employees to manage and perform certain HR-related tasks independently using technology and automation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/self-po.title: Self Policing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/self-po.description: Self-policing refers to actions taken by individuals or groups to monitor and regulate their own behavior without external oversight.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/self-fu.title: Self-funded Insurance Plan/ Self-insured Plan
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/self-fu.description: Self-funded Insurance Plan, also known as self-insured plan, is a type of health insurance in which an employer sets aside funds to pay for the medical claims of its employees, rather than purchasing a traditional insurance policy from an insurance company.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/retrenc.title: Retrenchment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/retrenc.description: Retrenchment refers to the process of reducing the size of a company’s workforce in order to cut costs and improve efficiency.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/retenti.title: Retention Strategy
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/retenti.description: Retention Strategy is a set of actions and practices to attract, engage, and retain employees. It includes steps such as identifying the problem, setting goals, conducting research, identifying retention factors, developing the strategy, communicating, implementing, monitoring and continuously improving.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/retenti.title: Retention
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/retenti.description: Retention refers to the ability of an organization to keep its employees over a period of time by implementing strategies such as competitive compensation, professional development, and employee engagement activities.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/retalia.title: Retaliation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/retalia.description: Retaliation refers to any adverse action taken against an individual for engaging in protected activity, such as reporting misconduct or opposing illegal practices. It is illegal and can have severe consequences for both the individual and the organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/self-fu.title: Self-Funded (Self-insured) Plan
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/self-fu.description: A self-funded plan is a type of healthcare plan where an employer sets aside funds to pay for employee healthcare expenses and assumes the financial risk for claims.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/second-.title: Second Chance Hiring
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/second-.description: Providing job opportunities to individuals with criminal records or past mistakes gives them a chance to reintegrate into society.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/search-.title: Search engine optimisation (SEO)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/search-.description: Search engine optimization (SEO) is the process of improving website visibility and ranking in search engine results.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/restric.title: Restrictive Covenant
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/restric.description: A Restrictive Covenant is a legal agreement that places limitations or restrictions on the use of a piece of property, and are included in deeds or other legal documents.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/schedul.title: Scheduled Time-off (planned leave)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/schedul.description: Scheduled time-off is pre-planned, agreed upon time off, including vacation, personal, and sick days.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/restric.title: Restricted Holidays
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/restric.description: Restricted Holidays are holidays specific to certain religions, ethnic groups or professions, recognized by some employers and not others.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/resourc.title: Resource Dependence Theory (RDT)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/resourc.description: Resource Dependence Theory (RDT) explains how organizations acquire and manage resources, and how this dependence affects their behavior, structure, and performance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/scalabi.title: Scalability
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/scalabi.description: Scalability is the ability of a system to handle an increasing amount of work or demand without a significant decline in performance or increase in cost.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/resigna.title: Resignation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/resigna.description: Resignation is the act of formally quitting employment, often due to dissatisfaction with pay, lack of opportunities, or poor management. It can have negative consequences such as loss of income and difficulty finding new employment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/residen.title: Resident Alien
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/residen.description: Resident Alien is a science fiction/comedy-drama series that premiered on Syfy in 2021 and is based on a comic book series of the same name. The show follows an alien who takes on the identity of a small-town human doctor.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/satisfi.title: Satisficing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/satisfi.description: Satisficing is a decision-making strategy in which an individual or organization settles for a satisfactory outcome instead of striving for the best possible one.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/salting.title: Salting
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/salting.description: Salting is a technique that adds a unique random string to a password before it is hashed, making it harder to crack by attackers.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/salary-.title: Salary Range
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/salary-.description: Salary range is pay offered for a job based on responsibilities, experience, qualifications, and market conditions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/safe-ha.title: Safe Harbor Regulations
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/safe-ha.description: Safe Harbor regulations are guidelines for companies to protect consumer data privacy; failure to comply may result in penalties such as fines, legal actions, and cease-and-desist orders.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/risk-ma.title: Risk management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/risk-ma.description: Risk management is identifying, assessing, and prioritizing risks to an organization and taking steps to mitigate or manage those risks.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/right-t.title: Right-to-Work State
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/right-t.description: A Right-to-Work state in the United States has laws prohibiting unions from requiring employees to pay union dues or fees as a condition of employment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sabbati.title: Sabbatical Leave
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sabbati.description: Sabbatical leave is an extended time off from work, typically unpaid, granted to employees for rest, travel, study, or research, often with a goal of personal development.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/right-t.title: Right to Sue Letter
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/right-t.description: A Right-to-Sue letter is a document issued by a government agency, such as the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) or the Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP).

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/rss-rea.title: RSS (Real Simple Syndication)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/rss-rea.description: RSS (Real Simple Syndication) is a way for users to subscribe to updates from websites, allowing for customized and organized news reading.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/right-t.title: Right to Work
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/right-t.description: The Right to Work is the legal principle allowing individuals to take employment without discrimination based on race, gender, religion, or national origin.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/right-t.title: Right to manage
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/right-t.description: What is the right to manage? The right to manage (RTM) is a legal right that allows tenants of a multi-unit building, such as a block of flats, to collectively take over the management of the building from the landlord. This includes responsibilities such as maintenance, repairs, insurance, and even appointment of managing agents. To…

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/request.title: Request For Proposal (RFP)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/request.description: A Request for Proposal (RFP) is a document used to solicit proposals from potential suppliers or vendors for a specific product or service. It outlines the requirements, specifications, and evaluation criteria to select a suitable vendor.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/rewards.title: Rewards And Recognition
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/rewards.description: Rewards and recognition is a practice that provides incentives and recognition to employees for their hard work, achievements, and contributions to the organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/reputat.title: Reputation Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/reputat.description: Reputation Management is the process of monitoring, identifying and influencing the perceptions of an individual, brand or company in the public sphere, to ensure a positive reputation and handle negative perceptions effectively.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/rotatio.title: Rotational Training
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/rotatio.description: Rotational training provides diverse skills, knowledge, and experiences but can be costly, time-consuming, and difficult to evaluate progress.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/reverse.title: Reverse mentoring: definition, benefits and guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/reverse.description: Reverse mentoring is a mentoring relationship where a less experienced employee, often a new hire or a junior employee, mentors a more experienced employee, typically a manager or executive.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/reporti.title: HR reporting suite: definition and guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/reporti.description: A Reporting Suite is a collection of tools that helps organizations analyze and create reports, which include data visualization, data analysis, data integration and scheduling features, allowing for better decision-making and improved communication.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/redunda.title: Redundancy
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/redunda.description: Redundancy refers to when an employee’s job is no longer needed; it can happen due to changes in the organization, a decrease in business, or the introduction of new technology.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/return-.title: Return on Investment (ROI)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/return-.description: It measures the profitability of an investment. It evaluates the efficiency of an investment by calculating the ratio of the net profit to the cost of the investment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/repetit.title: Repetitive strain injury (RSI): HR and OSHA guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/repetit.description: Repetitive Strain Injury (RSI) is an injury to the muscles, tendons, and nerves caused by repetitive motions. It can affect the hands, wrists, arms, shoulders, neck, and back. Symptoms include pain, numbness, and weakness.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/reducti.title: Reduction in force (RIF): process, legal guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/reducti.description: Reduction in Force (RIF) is a process where an employer reduces the number of employees through layoffs, early retirements, or downsizing, usually due to financial reasons.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/part-ti.title: Part-Time Employee
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/part-ti.description: A part-time employee is a worker who is employed for less than the standard full-time hours, and it generally ranges from 20 to 34 hours per week.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/red-cir.title: Red Circle Rate
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/red-cir.description: Red Circle Rate is a technology staffing and recruitment company that matches skilled professionals with clients quickly and efficiently.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/parkins.title: Parkinson’s law of triviality
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/parkins.description: Parkinson’s law of triviality is a concept that states that people spend a disproportionate amount of time and energy making decisions about small, insignificant details while neglecting important issues.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/recruit.title: Recruitment Software
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/recruit.description: Recruitment software automates the process of finding and hiring new employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/repatri.title: Repatriation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/repatri.description: Repatriation is the process of returning a person to their country of origin or citizenship, can be voluntary, involuntary, assisted, emergency or humanitarian.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pareto-.title: Pareto Principle
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pareto-.description: The Pareto principle, also known as the 80/20 rule, is a concept that states that in many situations, 80% of the effects come from 20% of the causes.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/recruit.title: Recruitment Process Outsourcing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/recruit.description: Outsourcing recruitment process to improve efficiency, quality of hires, and reduce costs.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/remuner.title: Remuneration
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/remuner.description: Remuneration refers to the total compensation an employee receives for their work, including monetary and non-monetary benefits.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/remote-.title: Remote Working
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/remote-.description: Remote Working is a work arrangement where employees perform their job duties from a location outside of the office, such as from home or another remote location.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pareto-.title: Pareto Chart
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pareto-.description: A Pareto chart is a type of chart that is used to identify and prioritize the most significant causes of a particular problem or issue.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/religio.title: Religious Accommodation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/religio.description: Religious Accommodation refers to adjustments made in the workplace to accommodate an employee’s sincerely held religious beliefs or practices, such as scheduling changes or dress code modifications.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/recruit.title: Recruitment Analytics
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/recruit.description: Recruitment analytics refers to the use of data and metrics to track and measure the recruitment process, allowing organizations to make data-driven decisions to improve their recruitment efforts.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/parent-.title: Parent-country nationals (PCNs)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/parent-.description: Parent-country nationals (PCNs) are employees of a multinational corporation (MNC) who are citizens of the company’s home or parent country.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/recruit.title: Recruitment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/recruit.description: Recruitment is the process of identifying, attracting, and hiring the best talent for open positions within an organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/parent-.title: Parent or Home country
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/parent-.description: A parent or home country refers to the country where a company was headquartered or established initially. It is the country where the company has its main office, management, and operations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/relievi.title: Relieving Letter
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/relievi.description: Relieving Letter is a document issued by an employer to an employee upon the termination of their employment, confirming the last day of work and reasons for departure.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/reasona.title: Reasonable Person Standard
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/reasona.description: The reasonable person standard is a legal principle used to determine if a person’s actions were reasonable and appropriate in a given situation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/outsour.title: Outsourcing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/outsour.description: Outsourcing refers to contracting with an external company or individual to perform a specific task or service that an internal employee or department would otherwise do.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/outplac.title: Outplacement
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/outplac.description: Outplacement services are a valuable resource for employees facing job loss and can help them find new employment and make a smooth transition to their next job.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/reasona.title: Reasonable Accommodation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/reasona.description: Reasonable accommodation refers to adjustments made for employees with disabilities to perform their job. Employers are responsible for providing these adjustments.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/regular.title: Regular Rate
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/regular.description: Regular Rate is the standard hourly rate for which an employee is paid, used to calculate overtime pay and ensure compliance with labor laws.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/osha-re.title: OSHA Recordkeeping and Reporting
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/osha-re.description: OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Administration) recordkeeping and reporting refer to maintaining accurate records of workplace injuries and illnesses and reporting specific incidents to OSHA.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/rationa.title: Rational legal Authority
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/rationa.description: Rational-legal authority is a form of governance in which power is based on legal and bureaucratic procedures to ensure fair and consistent decision-making.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/referen.title: Reference Letter
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/referen.description: A Reference Letter is a letter of recommendation written by someone to vouch for a job candidate’s qualifications, work ethic and character.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/orienta.title: Orientation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/orienta.description: In the context of organizations, orientation refers to introducing new employees to the organization, its culture, policies, and procedures.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/random-.title: Random Testing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/random-.description: Random testing is the selection of employees for testing at random intervals without notice.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/organiz.title: Organizational Semiotics
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/organiz.description: Organizational Semiotics can be used to Analyze the language and symbols used in corporate communication, such as in marketing, branding, and internal communications.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/random-.title: Random Drug Testing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/random-.description: Random drug testing is a type of drug testing conducted without prior notice to employees to detect and prevent drug use in the workplace.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/quid-pr.title: Quid Pro Quo Harassment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/quid-pr.description: Quid pro quo harassment is illegal form of workplace harassment where job benefits are linked to sexual favors or advances.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/queen-b.title: Queen Bee Syndrome
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/queen-b.description: Queen Bee Syndrome is when a female leader in the workplace discriminates against other women.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/organiz.title: Organizational Justice
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/organiz.description: Organizational justice refers to the perceived fairness of the treatment that employees receive from their organization. It encompasses three dimensions: distributive justice, procedural justice, and interactional justice.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/quantif.title: Quantified Self
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/quantif.description: Quantified Self refers to tracking and analyzing employee performance and well-being data to improve organizational performance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/quality.title: Quality Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/quality.description: Quality management is a systematic approach to ensuring products and services meet or exceed customer expectations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/organis.title: Organisational Development
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/organis.description: Organizational development (OD) improves an organization’s effectiveness by assessing and modifying its structure, processes, and culture.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/organiz.title: Organizational culture
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/organiz.description: Organizational culture refers to the shared values, beliefs, practices, customs, and social behaviors that characterize an organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/qualify.title: Qualifying Life Event
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/qualify.description: A Qualifying Life Event (QLE) is a specific event that allows individuals to make changes to their insurance coverage outside of the regular enrollment period.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/organiz.title: Organizational Change
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/organiz.description: Organizational change is modifying an organization’s structure, strategies, processes, or culture to improve performance or adapt to a changing environment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/qualifi.title: Qualified Medical Child Support Order (QMCSO)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/qualifi.description: QMCSO is a court order for the non-custodial parent to provide health insurance and pay for the child’s medical expenses.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/organic.title: Organic search results
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/organic.description: Organic search results refer to the unpaid or non-advertising search results that appear in search engines, such as Google, Bing, or Yahoo, when a user conducts a search query.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/open-bo.title: Open-book management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/open-bo.description: Open-book management is a business strategy that involves sharing financial and operational information with employees to increase transparency and accountability.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/qualifi.title: Qualified Domestic Relations Order (QDRO)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/qualifi.description: A Qualified Domestic Relations Order (QDRO) is a court order used to divide certain types of retirement benefits between divorced or separated spouses.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/psychom.title: Psychometric Test
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/psychom.description: Psychometric tests are standardized assessments used to evaluate an individual’s cognitive abilities, personality traits, skills, and attitudes to determine their suitability for a particular role.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/one-way.title: One-way interviews
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/one-way.description: One-way interviews, known as pre-recorded, are a type of interview where the candidate records their answers to a set of pre-determined questions and submits them to the employer for review.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/onboard.title: Onboarding
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/onboard.description: Onboarding is the process of integrating new employees into an organization, and it typically includes a range of activities and procedures to help new employees transition into their new roles.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/occupat.title: Occupational Prestige
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/occupat.description: Occupational prestige refers to the perceived status or respect associated with a particular occupation or profession.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/offer-l.title: Offer Letter
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/offer-l.description: An offer letter is a written document that an employer provides to a job candidate, outlining the terms and conditions of employment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/observa.title: Observation Interview
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/observa.description: An observation interview is a method of evaluating a candidate by observing their behavior, actions, and interactions in a specific situation or task.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/offshor.title: Offshoring
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/offshor.description: Offshoring refers to moving business operations, such as manufacturing, customer service, or research and development, from one company’s home country to another.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/objecti.title: Objectives And Key Results (OKR)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/objecti.description: Objectives and Key Results (OKR) is a goal setting framework that aligns organizational goals with individual employee goals; it provides measurable objectives and key results to track progress.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/offboar.title: Offboarding
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/offboar.description: Offboarding, also known as “separation management,” manages an employee’s exit from an organization. It’s an important process that helps to ensure a smooth transition for the employee and the company.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/onet-oc.title: O*Net (Occupational Information Network)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/onet-oc.description: O*Net (Occupational Information Network) is a database that provides detailed information on various occupations, used by HR professionals for job analysis, recruitment, career development, and workforce planning.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/occupat.title: Occupational Stress
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/occupat.description: Occupational stress refers to the physical and emotional responses when job demands exceed an individual’s coping ability. It can manifest in various ways, such as anxiety and other health problems.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/nut-isl.title: Nut Island Effect
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/nut-isl.description: The Nut Island Effect is a phenomenon where poor communication and coordination between teams leads to problems and inefficiencies in an organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/nonexem.title: Nonexempt Position
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/nonexem.description: A Nonexempt position is a job that is subject to labor laws such as overtime pay and minimum wage laws, and employees in this position are entitled to legal protections.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/occupat.title: Occupational Safety and Health Administration
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/occupat.description: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) is a federal agency within the United States Department of Labor responsible for ensuring employees’ safe and healthy working conditions by enforcing standards and regulations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/nonexem.title: Nonexempt Employee
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/nonexem.description: Nonexempt employees are those who are entitled to legal protections such as overtime pay and minimum wage laws, typically hourly workers.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/psychol.title: Psychological Contract
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/psychol.description: A Psychological Contract refers to the unwritten, perceived obligations and expectations between an employer and employee.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/protect.title: Protected Concerted Activity
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/protect.description: Protected Concerted Activity refers to the legal protection of employees’ rights to collectively advocate for better working conditions, wages, and benefits, promoting a fair and democratic workplace, free from retaliation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/protect.title: Protected Class
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/protect.description: Protected Class refers to a group of individuals protected from discrimination by law, based on characteristics such as race, sex, age, disability, and others, in areas such as employment, housing and education.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/progres.title: Progressive Discipline
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/progres.description: Progressive Discipline is a process for addressing and correcting unacceptable behavior or performance in the workplace, involving a series of increasingly severe consequences, with the goal of improvement without termination.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/profit-.title: Profit sharing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/profit-.description: Profit-sharing aligns employee incentives with company success, boosting morale and attracting talent, but can be difficult to implement and may create tension among employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/profess.title: Professional employer organization (PEO)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/profess.description: Professional Employer Organization (PEO) is a third-party service provider that acts as a co-employer of a company’s workers, providing services such as HR management, payroll, benefits administration, and liability and workers’ compensation insurance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/probati.title: Probationary arrangement
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/probati.description: Probationary Arrangement is a trial period of employment during which a new employee’s performance is evaluated by their employer, to ensure they are a good fit for the company and have necessary skills for the job.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/probati.title: Probation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/probati.description: Probation is a form of community supervision where an offender who has been convicted of a crime is released into the community under the supervision of a probation officer, rather than being incarcerated.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/princip.title: Principal agent problem
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/princip.description: Principal-Agent Problem is a problem that arises when an agent is entrusted to act on behalf of a principal, but their interests are not fully aligned which can lead to inefficiencies and reduced productivity.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/prince2.title: PRINCE2
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/prince2.description: PRINCE2 is a widely recognized project management methodology that provides a clear and organized framework for managing projects with defined roles, responsibilities, and a consistent approach.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/premium.title: Premium Only Plan (POP)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/premium.description: Premium Only Plan (POP) is a type of benefit plan that allows employers to set up a salary reduction agreement with their employees, under which employees can have a portion of their gross salary withheld and deposited into a pre-tax account, which can be used to pay for certain qualified benefit expenses.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/predict.title: Predictive Analytics
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/predict.description: Predictive Analytics is a process of using statistical and machine learning techniques to analyze historical data and make predictions about future events to help organizations make data-driven decisions and improve their operations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/positiv.title: Positive Discrimination
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/positiv.description: Positive Discrimination is a set of policies and practices aimed at increasing representation of underrepresented groups in areas where they have been historically excluded, providing equal opportunities and addressing historical discrimination and inequalities.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/positiv.title: Positive Culture and Respectful Workplace Survey
