https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/positiv.description: A Positive Culture and Respectful Workplace Survey is a tool used by organizations to assess employee engagement, job satisfaction, communication, teamwork, inclusivity, and fairness in the workplace, to identify areas of improvement and create a more positive and respectful work environment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/positio.title: Position Review
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/positio.description: Position Review is a process of evaluating the role and responsibilities of a job within an organization, identifying areas for improvement and aligning the position with the organization’s goals.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/positio.title: Position Description
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/positio.description: A Position Description is a document outlining the responsibilities, duties, and qualifications of a specific job within an organization, used for recruiting, legal compliance, performance evaluations, communication and career development.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/portfol.title: Portfolio Career
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/portfol.description: A Portfolio Career is one in which an individual has multiple jobs or income streams, rather than a traditional full-time job. It allows for flexibility, variety and the ability to pursue multiple passions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/platfor.title: Platform Economy
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/platfor.description: The Platform Economy uses digital platforms to connect individuals and businesses to exchange goods and services, creating new opportunities but also raising concerns about regulation, job security, and worker protections.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/plan-sp.title: Plan Sponsor
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/plan-sp.description: A plan Sponsor is the individual or organization that establishes and maintains a retirement plan for the benefit of its employees; responsible for design, compliance, administration and education for the plan.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/phased-.title: Phased Retirement
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/phased-.description: Phased Retirement allows employees to gradually reduce their work hours and responsibilities over time, to eventually transition into full retirement.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/peter-p.title: Peter Principle
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/peter-p.description: The Peter Principle states that employees will be promoted to their level of incompetence, leading to inefficiency and demotivation; organizations should use it to identify potential issues and improve management practices.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/personn.title: Personnel Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/personn.description: Personnel Management is responsible for recruiting, training, and developing employees, as well as managing employee relations, benefits, and compensation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/persona.title: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/persona.description: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) protects workers from hazards that can cause injury or death; it is often necessary in the workplace and required by OSHA regulations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/perform.title: Performance Based Pay
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/perform.description: Performance-based Pay links compensation to employee performance, motivates them to improve and aligns their interests with the organization’s goals.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/perform.title: Performance Review
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/perform.description: Performance Review is a process of evaluating an employee’s job performance, usually done by their supervisor or manager, to provide feedback, support, identify areas of improvement and opportunities for professional development, to help employees improve their performance and achieve organizational goals.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/perform.title: Performance Planning
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/perform.description: Performance Planning is the process of setting specific, measurable, and achievable performance goals for employees, in alignment with the organization’s objectives, to improve focus, productivity, and overall organizational performance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/perform.title: Performance Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/perform.description: Performance Management is a continuous process of setting goals, monitoring progress, providing feedback and support, and evaluating and rewarding performance to improve organizational and employee performance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/perform.title: Performance Appraisal
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/perform.description: Performance Appraisal is the process of evaluating an employee’s job performance, usually done by their supervisor or manager, to provide feedback and support to improve performance and achieve organizational goals.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/nondisc.title: Nondiscrimination Testing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/nondisc.description: Nondestructive testing (NDT) is a method of evaluating the properties of a material or component without causing damage, used to detect defects, measure properties, and determine integrity.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/nondisc.title: Nondiscretionary Bonus
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/nondisc.description: A non-discretionary bonus is a type of bonus based on set formula or criteria and not on employer discretion, typically outlined in the employee’s contract or company’s policies.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/people-.title: People Analytics
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/people-.description: People Analytics is the use of data and analytics to understand and manage the workforce in an organization, providing insights to improve decision-making, increase efficiency, and optimize workforce strategy, but also raises concerns about data privacy and limited scope.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/people/.title: People
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/people/.description: People are the driving force behind an organization, bringing skills, perspectives, and energy to the workforce, fulfilling job duties, meeting performance expectations and representing the company professionally, key to achieving organizational goals.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/noncomp.title: Noncompete Agreement
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/noncomp.description: A noncompete agreement is a legal contract in which an individual agrees not to work for a competing company for a certain period of time.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/peer-ap.title: Peer Appraisal
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/peer-ap.description: Peer Appraisal is a process where employees evaluate the performance of their colleagues through self-assessments, 360-degree evaluations, or peer evaluations providing feedback, identifying areas for improvement, fostering open communication and continuous improvement.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/non-tra.title: NonTraditional Employment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/non-tra.description: Non-traditional employment refers to jobs where underrepresented groups like women, minorities, and people with disabilities constitute less than 25% of the workforce.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/payroll.title: Payroll Software Service
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/payroll.description: Payroll Software Service automates and streamlines the process of paying employees, ensuring compliance, accurate record keeping, generating reports, and tracking employee data and hours, helping businesses manage payroll effectively.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/non-tra.title: Non Tradition Employee Benefits vs Traditional Employee Benefits
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/non-tra.description: Non-traditional benefits are perks outside of the standard health, retirement, and paid time off, while traditional benefits include those standard offerings.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/non-dis.title: Non Disclosure Agreement
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/non-dis.description: A non-disclosure agreement (NDA) is a legal contract between two parties in which one party agrees to not disclose confidential information shared by the other party.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/newsjac.title: Newsjacking
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/newsjac.description: Newsjacking is the practice of using current events to promote a company’s brand and increase its visibility as a thought leader in its industry.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/payroll.title: Payroll Software
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/payroll.description: Payroll Software automates the process of calculating, distributing and managing employee pay, taxes, and benefits, saving time, reducing errors, and ensuring compliance with regulations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/new-hir.title: New Hire Reporting
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/new-hir.description: New Hire Reporting is the process of reporting new employees to state agencies for child support enforcement.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/payroll.title: Payroll Processing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/payroll.description: Payroll Processing automates the calculation and distribution of employee salaries, taxes, and benefits, saving time and reducing errors. However, it can come with costs and potential for inaccuracies if not properly managed.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/net-sal.title: Net Salary
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/net-sal.description: Net salary is the amount of money an employee receives after all deductions, such as taxes, insurance, and retirement contributions, have been subtracted from their gross salary.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/nepotis.title: Nepotism
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/nepotis.description: Nepotism is the practice of showing favoritism to friends and family members in the workplace, often involving hiring or promotions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/negotia.title: Negotiation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/negotia.description: Negotiation is a process of communication with the aim of reaching an agreement or understanding through discussion and compromise.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/neglige.title: Negligent Retention
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/neglige.description: Negligent retention is the failure of an employer to terminate an employee when they knew or should have known that the employee posed a danger to others.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/neglige.title: Negligent Referral
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/neglige.description: Negligent referral is when an employer refers an employee to a third party, knowing or having reason to know that the employee poses a risk of harm, and the employee subsequently causes harm to the third party.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/neglige.title: Negligent Hiring
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/neglige.description: Negligent hiring refers to an employer’s failure to properly screen job candidates, resulting in harm to a third party.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/natural.title: Natural-language processing (NLP)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/natural.description: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a branch of AI that enables machines to understand and interpret human language.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/payroll.title: Payroll Outsourcing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/payroll.description: Payroll outsourcing is the process of hiring an external company to handle all or part of a business’s payroll function to save time, money and ensure compliance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/payroll.title: Payroll
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/payroll.description: Payroll is the process of paying employees for their time and work, including calculating and distributing salaries, wages, bonuses, and deductions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pay-per.title: Pay-per-impression
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pay-per.description: Pay-per-impression (PPI) is an advertising model where an advertiser pays each time an ad is displayed, regardless of clicks or conversions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pay-per.title: Pay-per-click (PPC)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pay-per.description: Pay-per-click (PPC) is a form of online advertising where advertisers pay a fee each time their ad is clicked, it’s a cost-effective way to drive traffic to a website, highly trackable, target specific demographics, flexible and gives a competitive edge, it’s an ongoing process that requires optimization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pay-ran.title: Pay Range
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pay-ran.description: Pay Range is a set of minimum and maximum pay rates for a specific job or group of jobs, it’s used to determine the pay rate, ensure fairness, facilitate budgeting, internal equity, external competitiveness, career progression, compliance and improve employee retention.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pay-gra.title: Pay Grade
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pay-gra.description: Pay Grade is a system to classify and group jobs within an organization based on their relative level of difficulty, responsibility, and skill, it includes a set of pay ranges for each grade and it is used to determine the pay rate for each job, it facilitates budgeting, internal equity, career progression and compliance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pay-equ.title: Pay Equity
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pay-equ.description: Pay Equity refers to ensuring that employees are paid the same amount for doing the same or similar work, regardless of their gender, race, religion, age, disability, or other protected characteristics. It’s a principle of fairness and legal compliance, achieved through analyzing, comparing and adjusting pay for similar jobs.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pay-com.title: Pay Compression
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/pay-com.description: Pay Compression is a situation where the pay difference between employees with similar qualifications and experience becomes smaller, leading to lower employee morale, difficulty in retention and recruitment, inequities, decreased productivity, legal issues and negative impact on brand reputation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/passive.title: Passive Candidate
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/passive.description: Passive Candidates are currently employed and not actively looking for a new job, but open to new opportunities, they bring in specialized skills, long-term tenure, better qualifications, referred by current employees and low-cost recruitment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/narciss.title: Narcissistic Leadership
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/narciss.description: Narcissistic Leadership is a leadership style characterized by excessive self-absorption, self-centeredness, and arrogance, putting own interests above the organization’s, which can lead to negative consequences for the organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/myers-b.title: Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/myers-b.description: Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI) is a psychological assessment tool that determines an individual’s personality type based on preferences in four dichotomies: Extraversion-Introversion, Sensing-Intuition, Thinking-Feeling, and Judging-Perceiving.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/multite.title: Multitenant
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/multite.description: Multitenancy is a software architecture that allows multiple customers to share the same software instance, enabling cost savings and improved efficiency.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/motivat.title: Motivational Theories
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/motivat.description: Motivational Theories is a product of three beliefs: Expectancy (if I try, can I succeed?), Instrumentality (if I succeed, will I receive a reward?), and Valence (do I value that reward?). What is motivational theories? Motivational theories aim to understand what drives individuals within a group to be motivated. Companies are interested in this because…

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/morale/.title: Morale
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/morale/.description: Morale refers to the emotional and psychological well-being of individuals within an organization, it is a measure of their level of satisfaction and engagement with their work, their colleagues, and the organization as a whole.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mooc-ma.title: MOOC (Massive Open Online Course)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mooc-ma.description: MOOC (Massive Open Online Course) is a type of online course that is open to anyone, anywhere, and typically offered at no cost, it uses technology to deliver high-quality education to large numbers of people.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/momtrep.title: Momtrepreneur
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/momtrep.description: Momtrepreneur is a term used to describe mothers who are also entrepreneurs, they combine their roles as mothers with running their own business, they are often seen as an inspiration for balancing work and family life.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mohawk-.title: Mohawk Valley Formula
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mohawk-.description: The Mohawk Valley Formula is a method for determining the value of a business, it compares the business’s net income to the value of its tangible assets and uses this ratio to establish a fair market value for the company.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mobile-.title: Mobile Working
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mobile-.description: Mobile Working is the practice of working outside of a traditional office, it allows employees to work from any location using laptops, smartphones, and other mobile devices, it increases flexibility and productivity.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mobile-.title: Mobile Recruiting
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mobile-.description: Mobile Recruiting is the process of using mobile devices and technologies to attract, engage, and hire job candidates, it includes using mobile-friendly career websites, social media, text messaging, and mobile job applications.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mission.title: Mission Statement
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mission.description: A Mission Statement is a statement of purpose that outlines an organization’s goals, values, and objectives, and communicates its overall strategy and approach. It defines the organization’s reason for existence.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/minorit.title: Minority Business Enterprise (MBE)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/minorit.description: Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) is a business that is at least 51% owned, operated and controlled by one or more minorities, such as African Americans, Hispanic Americans, and Asian-Pacific Americans, among others.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/minimum.title: Minimum Wage
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/minimum.description: Minimum Wage is the lowest amount of pay that an employer can legally pay to an employee for their work, it is set by the government and is usually reviewed and adjusted periodically.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/millenn.title: Millennials
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/millenn.description: Millennials, also known as Generation Y, are individuals born between 1981 and 1996. They are known for their use of technology and social media, as well as their attitudes towards work and life balance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mid-ran.title: Mid-Range Wage
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mid-ran.description: Mid-range Wage refers to a salary that falls between the lowest and highest wages in a particular group of employees, it is considered as a benchmark or a standard wage for a specific job or profession.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labour-.title: Labour Force Participation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labour-.description: What is labour force participation? Labour Force Participation is refers to the proportion of a country’s working-age population (typically aged 15-64 or 16-64) that is either employed or actively seeking employment. The calculation of labour force participation is done by taking the number of individuals who are either employed or unemployed but actively seeking employment,…

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/matrix-.title: Matrix Organization
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/matrix-.description: A Matrix Organization is a structure in which employees report to multiple managers and work on multiple projects simultaneously.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/marketi.title: Marketing Public Relations
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/marketi.description: Marketing Public Relations (PR) is the use of media and communication tactics to enhance a company’s reputation and build positive relationships with stakeholders.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mandato.title: Mandatory Benefits
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mandato.description: Mandatory benefits are minimum benefits required by law to be provided to employees by employers, such as minimum wage, social security, unemployment insurance, etc.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/managem.title: Management Training
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/managem.description: Management training is education and development for individuals to improve their skills in managing teams and organizations effectively.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/managem.title: Management Styles
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/managem.description: Management styles refer to approaches to decision-making and leadership, such as autocratic, democratic, and laissez-faire.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/managem.title: Management by Objective
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/managem.description: Management by Objectives is a goal-oriented management approach that involves setting specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound goals.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/managem.title: Management Bandwidth
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/managem.description: Management bandwidth refers to the amount of time and mental capacity a manager has for focusing on tasks and responsibilities.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/micro-m.title: Micro-management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/micro-m.description: Micro-management is a management style where a manager closely monitors and controls the work of their subordinates, often involving excessive oversight and frequent check-ins, which can lead to low employee morale and poor performance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/metrics.title: Metrics
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/metrics.description: Metrics are quantitative measurements that are used to evaluate and track the performance, progress, or success of a specific aspect of a business, organization, or project.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/merit-p.title: Merit Pay
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/merit-p.description: Merit pay, also known as performance related pay or pay-for-performance, is a system of compensating employees based on their individual performance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mentor/.title: Mentor
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mentor/.description: A Mentor is an experienced and trusted advisor who guides, advises and supports an individual, usually in a professional or educational setting, helping them to develop their skills, knowledge and career.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/medical.title: Medical Savings Account (MSA)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/medical.description: A Medical Savings Account (MSA) is a type of savings account that is paired with a high-deductible health plan (HDHP) and is used to pay for qualified medical expenses.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mediati.title: Mediation Services
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mediati.description: Mediation Services are a form of alternative dispute resolution where a neutral third party helps to facilitate communication and negotiate a mutually acceptable solution between disputing parties.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/median-.title: Median Wage
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/median-.description: Median Wage refers to the salary that separates the top half of workers from the bottom half, it is the middle point of a dataset, where 50% of the workers earn more and 50% earn less.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mean-wa.title: Mean Wage
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mean-wa.description: Mean Wage refers to the average salary earned by a group of employees, calculated by dividing the total sum of all salaries by the number of employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mcommer.title: mCommerce
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/mcommer.description: mCommerce, or mobile commerce, refers to buying and selling goods or services through mobile devices such as smartphones or tablets.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/layoff/.title: Layoff
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/layoff/.description: A Layoff is a temporary or permanent termination of employment, typically due to economic conditions or a change in the employer’s needs.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/managed.title: Managed Service Provider
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/managed.description: A company that manages and assumes responsibility for providing a specific service, such as IT support, to its clients.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/managed.title: Managed Care
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/managed.description: A healthcare delivery system that aims to control costs and improve quality through coordinated care and cost containment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/machine.title: Machine Learning
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/machine.description: A subfield of artificial intelligence that allows systems to automatically improve from experience without being explicitly programmed.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/lump-su.title: Lump Sum Payment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/lump-su.description: A single, one-time payment for a specific amount.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/loyalty.title: Loyalty Programs
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/loyalty.description: Loyalty programs are incentives offered by businesses to encourage repeat customers, typically through points, rewards, and special promotions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/long-te.title: Long-term Care Insurance
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/long-te.description: Long-term care insurance is a type of insurance coverage that helps pay for costs associated with long-term care services, such as nursing home or in-home care.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/lockste.title: Lockstep Compensation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/lockste.description: Lockstep compensation is a method of determining employee salaries in which all employees within a certain level or job class are paid the same amount.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/living-.title: Living Wage
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/living-.description: A living wage is an amount of money considered necessary to meet basic needs and maintain a decent standard of living.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/lifo-la.title: LIFO (last in, first out)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/lifo-la.description: LIFO (Last In, First Out) is a method of organizing and manipulating data in which the last item entered is the first item to be removed.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/leave-m.title: Leave Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/leave-m.description: Leave management is the process of tracking, approving, and managing employee time off requests, including vacation, sick days, and personal time.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/learnin.title: Learning Style
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/learnin.description: A learning style is a preferred method of acquiring, processing, and retaining information, determined by individual characteristics and experiences.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/learnin.title: Learning Management System (LMS)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/learnin.description: A Learning Management System (LMS) is a software platform for delivering, tracking, and managing e-learning and training programs.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/learnin.title: Learning and Development
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/learnin.description: Learning and Development refers to the process of acquiring new knowledge, skills and abilities to enhance personal and professional growth.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/leaders.title: Leadership Development
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/leaders.description: Leadership development is the process of improving and honing one’s leadership skills and abilities, typically through a combination of training, coaching, and experience.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/last-in.title: Last In, First Out (LIFO)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/last-in.description: Last In, First Out (LIFO) is a method of organizing data where the last item added is the first item to be removed. It is commonly used in stack data structures.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labour-.title: Labour Union
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labour-.description: Labor Union is an organization of workers that aims to protect the rights and interests of its members through collective bargaining, advocacy, and other means.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labour-.title: Labour Market
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labour-.description: Labour Market is the place where workers and employers interact to hire labour, it determines wages, benefits, and working conditions of employees and the cost of labour for employers.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labour-.title: Labour Force Participation Rate
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labour-.description: Labour Force Participation Rate is the percentage of the working-age population that is either employed or actively seeking employment. It is a measure of the active portion of an economy’s labour force.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-rot.title: Job Rotation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-rot.description: Job rotation refers to the practice of moving employees from one job or role to another within an organization, typically to develop and broaden their skills and experience.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labor-f.title: Labor Force
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labor-f.description: Labor Force refers to the number of people employed or seeking employment in an economy.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labor-c.title: Labor Certification
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labor-c.description: Labor Certification is a process in which an employer seeks to employ a foreign worker for a specific job opportunity in the United States, ensuring that it won’t adversely affect U.S workers, providing legal basis for hiring foreign workers and it is a prerequisite for certain types of green card applications.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/knowled.title: Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/knowled.description: Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs) are the attributes that an individual must possess to perform a particular job or task, including knowledge, skills, and natural talents or aptitudes.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/knowled.title: Knowledge based Pay
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/knowled.description: Knowledge-based Pay is a type of compensation system in which an employee’s pay is based on their knowledge, skills, and abilities, aligning employee compensation with organizational goals and motivating employees to develop new skills.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/knowled.title: Knowledge Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/knowled.description: Knowledge Management is the process of acquiring, creating, sharing, and using knowledge to improve performance, competitiveness, and innovation within an organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/key-res.title: Key Result Areas
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/key-res.description: Key Result Areas (KRA) are a set of specific, measurable, and time-bound goals that align with organizational objectives, used to improve performance, set clear expectations and facilitate communication.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/key-per.title: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/key-per.description: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are measurable values used to evaluate performance, aligned with goals, used to identify areas for improvement, monitor progress, facilitate communication and make data-driven decisions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/key-emp.title: Key Employee
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/key-emp.description: Key Employees are considered valuable assets to an organization, due to their skills, knowledge, and unique qualities. They are critical to the success of the organization and their loss can have a significant impact.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labor-l.title: Labor Law Posting
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labor-l.description: Labor law posting refers to the legal requirement to display certain labor laws and regulations in the workplace.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/just-ca.title: Just Cause Termination
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/just-ca.description: Just cause termination is the dismissal of an employee for valid, evidence-based reasons, ensuring the action is neither arbitrary nor discriminatory.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/john-he.title: John Henry Effect
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/john-he.description: The John Henry Effect is a phenomenon where people are more likely to persist at a task when they are in competition with a machine, it highlights the psychological and social factors that can influence people’s perceptions and reactions to technology.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-dis.title: Job Dissatisfaction
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-dis.description: Job dissatisfaction is a feeling of unhappiness or frustration with one’s current employment, caused by a variety of factors such as poor management, lack of opportunities, low compensation and more.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-ref.title: Job Reference Immunity Statutes
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-ref.description: Job reference immunity statutes, also known as “reference immunity” laws, provide immunity or protection to employers or former employers from liability when providing job references for current or former employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-eva.title: Job Evaluation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-eva.description: Job evaluation is a systematic process of determining the relative worth of different organizational jobs.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-des.title: Job Description
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-des.description: A document outlining the duties, responsibilities, and qualifications of a specific role within a company.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-ana.title: Job Analysis
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-ana.description: Job Analysis is the process of gathering information about a specific job to identify duties, skills, and qualifications required.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-poli.title: HR Policies
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-poli.description: HR Policies provide guidance and structure for employee treatment, decision-making, and expectations, ensuring fair treatment, legal compliance, and positive work environment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/iso-900.title: ISO 9001, 9004
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/iso-900.description: ISO 9001 is an international standard for quality management systems (QMS).ISO 9004 is a set of guidelines for performance improvement that organizations of any type or size can use.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/accommo.title: Accommodation Network (JAN)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/accommo.description: JAN is a free service that offers information on workplace accommodations for people with disabilities, under ADA laws.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-mana.title: HR Manager
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-mana.description: HR Manager is responsible for overseeing and implementing an organization’s human resources strategy, including recruiting, employee relations, compliance, training and talent management.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-info.title: HR Information Systems
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-info.description: HR Information Systems (HRIS) automate and manage HR functions, such as data management, compliance, recruitment and performance management, to increase efficiency and productivity.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/iso-900.title: ISO 9001
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/iso-900.description: ISO 9001 is a standard that provides the requirements for an organization’s quality management system (QMS).

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-gene.title: HR Generalist
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-gene.description: HR Generalist is responsible for recruiting, onboarding, employee relations, benefits administration, compliance and talent management.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/insubor.title: Insubordination
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/insubor.description: Insubordination is the act of refusing to obey or comply with orders or instructions from a supervisor, which can lead to disciplinary action or termination of employment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-dire.title: HR Director
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-dire.description: HR Director manages and oversees the human resources department of an organization, responsible for recruiting, employee relations, compliance and fostering a positive work environment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/instruc.title: Instructional Design
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/instruc.description: Instructional design is the process of creating educational or training materials and activities in a systematic way, including analyzing learning needs, designing and developing instructional materials, and evaluating their effectiveness.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/iso-900.title: ISO 9000
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/iso-900.description: ISO 9001 provides the requirements for a quality management system. Organizations demonstrate that they have a system to ensure that their products and services exceed customer and other stakeholder requirements.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/interns.title: Internship
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/interns.description: An internship is a period of work experience offered by an organization for a limited period. Internships are commonly offered in business, engineering, technology, healthcare, media, and education.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-depa.title: HR Department
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-depa.description: HR Department is responsible for managing and coordinating human resources functions within an organization, including recruitment, employee relations, compliance, and training.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/inpatri.title: Inpatriate
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/inpatri.description: Inpatriate: An employee from a foreign subsidiary assigned to work in the company’s home country, bringing international insights to local operations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-cons.title: HR Consulting
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-cons.description: HR Consulting provides expert advice and guidance to organizations on various aspects of human resources management, including recruitment, employee relations, compliance and helping organizations achieve their business goals.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/injunct.title: Injunctive Relief
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/injunct.description: Injunctive relief is a legal remedy that prohibits or orders specific actions and can offer other forms of relief.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-comp.title: HR Compliance
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-comp.description: HR Compliance refers to the adherence to laws and regulations related to the management of employees and their rights, ensuring fair treatment and protecting the company from legal action and penalties.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/informa.title: Informal Communication
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/informa.description: Informal communication refers to casual, unofficial conversations and interactions that take place in the workplace, apart from official channels.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/industr.title: Industrial Relations
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/industr.description: Industrial Relations refers to the relationship between employers, employees and the government in the workplace. It encompasses issues such as collective bargaining, labor laws, and workplace disputes.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/interne.title: Internet of Things (IoT) in HR: workplace guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/interne.description: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of physical devices, vehicles, buildings, and other objects embedded with sensors, software, and connectivity, enabling these objects to collect and exchange data.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/industr.title: Industrial Psychology
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/industr.description: Industrial psychology is the scientific study of human behavior in the workplace to improve employee performance and organizational effectiveness.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/interna.title: International Labour Organization: HR guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/interna.description: The ILO’s work is guided by its Constitution, which states that its purpose is to promote rights at work, and employment opportunities, enhance social protection and strengthen dialogue on work-related issues.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/industr.title: Industrial and organizational psychology: HR guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/industr.description: Industrial-Organizational psychology is the scientific study of human behavior in the workplace and the application of this knowledge to improve employee performance and organizational effectiveness.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/interna.title: International HRM: definition, approaches and guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/interna.description: International Human Resource Management (IHRM) refers to managing human resources in a global context. It involves strategically managing an organization’s human capital to align with its global mission.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/intelle.title: Intellectual property in HR: employment guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/intelle.description: Intellectual property (IP) refers to creations of the mind, such as inventions, literary and artistic works, symbols, names, images, and designs used in commerce.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/intangi.title: Intangible Rewards
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/intangi.description: Intangible rewards are non-monetary recognition or incentives provided to employees in addition to their salary or wages.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/integri.title: Integrity Testing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/integri.description: Integrity testing, also known as honesty testing, is a method used to assess the honesty and integrity of job applicants or employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/inducti.title: Induction
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/inducti.description: Induction is the process of introducing and orienting new employees to an organization’s culture, policies, and procedures.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/individ.title: Individual Employment Agreement
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/individ.description: An individual employment agreement is a legal contract outlining the terms and conditions of the employment relationship between an employer and an employee.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/individ.title: Individual Coverage Health Reimbursement Account (ICHRA)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/individ.description: An Individual Coverage Health Reimbursement Arrangement (ICHRA) is a type of health benefit plan that allows employers to reimburse employees for their health insurance premiums and out-of-pocket medical expenses.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hybrid-.title: Hybrid Organization
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hybrid-.description: A hybrid organization is a type of organizational structure that combines elements of traditional and decentralized structures to increase flexibility and adaptability.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/indepen.title: Independent contractor
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/indepen.description: An independent contractor is a self-employed individual or business that provides goods or services to another business or individual.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-r.title: Human Resources Analytics
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-r.description: Human Resources Analytics is the process of using data and statistical analysis to inform and improve decision-making in HR management.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/indirec.title: Indirect compensation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/indirec.description: Indirect compensation refers to the benefits and perks an employee receives in addition to their salary or wages.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-r.title: Human Resource Planning
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-r.description: Human Resource Planning is the process of forecasting and meeting future personnel needs.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/inclusi.title: Inclusion
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/inclusi.description: Inclusion is an ongoing process requiring everyone in an organization or community to create a culture of respect, fairness, and inclusiveness.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-r.title: Human Resource Outsourcing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-r.description: Human Resource Outsourcing is the process of delegating certain HR functions to an external provider.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/inciden.title: Incidence rate
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/inciden.description: The incidence rate measures the frequency of new cases of a particular disease or condition within a specific population over a certain period.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-r.title: Human Resources Management System (HRMS)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-r.description: A Human Resources Management System (HRMS) is a software system that automates and streamlines various HR functions and enables data-driven decisions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/incenti.title: Incentive pay
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/incenti.description: Incentive pay, also known as performance pay or pay-for-performance, is a type of compensation where an employee’s pay is directly tied to their performance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/in-hous.title: In-house solutions
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/in-hous.description: In-house solutions refer to products, services, or systems developed and managed by a company or organization for its use rather than outsourcing the development or management to a third-party vendor.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-r.title: Human Resource Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-r.description: Human Resource Management (HRM) is the process of managing an organization’s employees; involving recruiting, hiring, training, and managing personnel while ensuring compliance with labor laws.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-r.title: Human Resource Information System
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-r.description: A Human Resource Information System (HRIS) is a system used to collect, store, and manage data on an organization’s employees. It automates HR tasks and provides data for informed decision-making.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/imputed.title: Imputed Income
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/imputed.description: Imputed income is income assigned to an individual or entity by a government agency or court, even though it was not earned or received.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-r.title: Human Relations Movement
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-r.description: The human relations movement focuses on employee satisfaction, motivation, and effective communication to improve workplace relationships and productivity.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/imputed.title: Implicit Bias
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/imputed.description: Implicit bias is unconscious attitudes, beliefs, and stereotypes that influence an individual’s perceptions, decisions, and actions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-c.title: Human Capital Management Software-as-a-Service (HCM SaaS)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-c.description: Human Capital Management Software-as-a-Service (HCM SaaS) is a software-based service to manage human resources over the internet.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-c.title: Human Capital Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-c.description: Human Capital Management (HCM) is the process of acquiring, developing, managing, and optimizing the human resources of an organization to achieve its strategic goals.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-c.title: Human Capital
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/human-c.description: Human capital refers to the knowledge, skills, abilities and other attributes of a workforce that can be used to generate economic value and improve organizational performance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-soft.title: HR Software
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-soft.description: HR software is a set of tools designed to automate and streamline human resources management tasks, such as recruitment, employee data management, performance evaluations, payroll, benefits administration and compliance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-serv.title: HR Service Delivery
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-serv.description: HR Service Delivery refers to the systems and processes used by HR departments to provide services to employees and managers.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-busi.title: HR Business Partner
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-busi.description: HR Business Partners (HRBP) aligns organization’s human resources strategies with overall business objectives, acting as a liaison between HR and the rest of the organization and provides guidance and support on a wide range of issues.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-audi.title: HR Audit
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-audi.description: HR Audit is a systematic review of an organization’s human resources policies, procedures and practices to evaluate effectiveness, compliance and identify areas for improvement.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/health-.title: Health Care Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/health-.description: Health Care Flexible Spending Account (FSA) is a benefit that allows employees to set aside pre-tax income to pay for out-of-pocket medical expenses through payroll deductions, claims submission and reimbursement.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hawthor.title: Hawthorne Effect
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hawthor.description: The Hawthorne Effect refers to individuals changing behavior as a result of being observed, leading to inaccurate conclusions in research and improved productivity in organizations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hostile.title: Hostile Work Environment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hostile.description: A hostile work environment is a workplace that is made hostile or intimidating due to discriminatory or harassing behavior.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/harassm.title: Harassment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/harassm.description: Harassment is unwanted and unwarranted behavior that creates a hostile environment, stemming from prejudice or bias, causing emotional distress, physical or mental health issues, and legal action.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/horizon.title: Horizontal Organization
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/horizon.description: A horizontal organization has few management layers and distributed decision-making. See vs vertical structure, HR career design, compensation, and holacracy.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/halo-ef.title: Halo Effect
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/halo-ef.description: The halo effect is a cognitive bias where one positive trait inflates overall judgment. See hiring bias, horn effect, performance review, and interview fixes.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/high-po.title: High Potential Employee (HiPo)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/high-po.description: High-potential employees (HiPos) identified for accelerated leadership development. See identification criteria, 9-box grid, HiPo programs, and retention.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/h-1b-vi.title: H-1B Visa
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/h-1b-vi.description: H-1B visa lets US employers hire in specialty occupations. See annual cap, lottery process, LCA, employer obligations, and visa alternatives.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/high-re.title: High Reliability Organisation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/high-re.description: High reliability organisations prevent failures in high-hazard domains. See 5 Weick-Sutcliffe principles, healthcare HRO, HR’s role, and reliability measures.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hierarc.title: Hierarchy of Needs
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hierarc.description: Maslow’s hierarchy arranges needs from physiological to self-actualization. See 5 levels, expanded model, HR motivation applications, and employee engagement.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-anal.title: HR Analytics
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-anal.description: HR analytics is the process of using data and statistical methods to measure human resources-related data. This data includes information on employee turnover, recruitment, training, performance, and many other areas.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hidden-.title: Hidden Job Market
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hidden-.description: The hidden job market refers to job opportunities that are not publicly advertised and can be found through networking, employee referrals, or recruitment services.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/group-d.title: Group Dynamics
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/group-d.description: Group Dynamics is the study of the processes and behaviors that occur within a group of people, it encompasses the ways in which group members interact, communicate, and make decisions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-asso.title: HR Associate
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-asso.description: HR Associate is a junior-level position that provides support to the HR department and helps with the implementation of HR policies and procedures.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-assi.title: HR Assistant
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/hr-assi.description: An HR Assistant is a junior-level position that supports the HR department and helps implement HR policies and procedures.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gross-s.title: Gross Salary
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gross-s.description: Gross Salary is the total amount of money an employee earns before any deductions or taxes have been taken out, it includes basic salary, overtime pay, bonuses, and other forms of compensation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gross-m.title: Gross Misconduct
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gross-m.description: Gross Misconduct is a serious violation of an employer’s rules or policies, or a serious breach of an employee’s contract of employment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/health-.title: Health Savings Account
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/health-.description: A Health Savings Account (HSA) is a savings account that is linked to a high-deductible health plan (HDHP) and offers tax benefits for employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/grievan.title: Grievance
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/grievan.description: A Grievance is a complaint or issue raised by an employee with their employer, usually related to work or working conditions, and the process of addressing a grievance typically involves steps such as investigation, meeting, and appeal.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gratuit.title: Gratuity
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gratuit.description: Gratuity is a monetary benefit paid to employees upon termination of their employment, usually as a recognition and reward for long-term service and dedication to a company.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/health-.title: Health Reimbursement Account (HRA)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/health-.description: A Health Reimbursement Account (HRA) is an employer-funded account used to pay for eligible medical expenses, such as deductibles, copayments, and prescriptions, with reimbursements being tax-free.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/generat.title: Generation Y
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/generat.description: Generation Y, also known as Gen Y or the Millennial generation, refers to the demographic cohort of individuals born between the early 1980s and the mid-1990s to early 2000s.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/good-fa.title: Good Faith Bargaining
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/good-fa.description: Good Faith Bargaining refers to the process of negotiating in a fair and honest manner, with the goal of reaching a mutually beneficial agreement.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/health-.title: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/health-.description: HIPAA is a US law that protects health information privacy & security, also helps maintain health insurance during job changes.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/generat.title: Generation X
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/generat.description: Generation X, also known as Gen X, refers to the demographic cohort of individuals born between the mid-1960s and the early-1980s.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/general.title: General manager
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/general.description: A General Manager (GM) is a high-level executive responsible for a business or organization’s overall operations and performance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/golden-.title: Golden Parachute
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/golden-.description: Golden Parachute is a type of severance package offered to top executives of a company in the event of a merger, acquisition, or other change of control, it can provide financial security but also can have a negative impact on company’s financials.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/goals-g.title: Goals/Goal Setting
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/goals-g.description: Goal setting is the process of defining and planning specific, measurable, attainable, relevant, and time-bound objectives to help individuals and organizations achieve desired outcomes.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/golden-.title: Golden Handshake
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/golden-.description: A Golden Handshake is a financial incentive offered to an employee as part of a severance package when they leave a company, usually as a result of retirement, redundancy or early retirement.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/global-.title: Global Human Resource Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/global-.description: GHRM is the process of managing the recruitment, selection, and management of an organization’s human resources on a global scale, including managing cultural and legal differences across countries and regions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/golden-.title: Golden Handcuffs
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/golden-.description: Golden Handcuffs are incentives offered by an employer to retain employees, they can retain valuable employees but can also limit employee mobility and motivation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/goldbri.title: Goldbricking
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/goldbri.description: Goldbricking refers to avoiding work or shirking responsibilities, it can lead to decreased productivity, reduced job satisfaction and damage to reputation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/glass-c.title: Glass Ceiling
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/glass-c.description: The invisible barrier that prevents women and minorities from advancing to higher-level positions within a company or organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gig-wor.title: Gig Worker
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gig-wor.description: A gig worker is an individual who works on a project-by-project or task-by-task basis, not considered traditional employees and often work as independent contractors, freelancers, or temporary workers.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/what-is.title: GIG Economy
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/what-is.description: The gig economy is a labor market characterized by the prevalence of short-term contracts or freelance work as opposed to permanent jobs.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/ghent-s.title: Ghent System
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/ghent-s.description: The Ghent System is a method of providing unemployment benefits through trade unions, primarily used in Denmark, Iceland, Finland and Sweden, with benefits based on previous earnings.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/general.title: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/general.description: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) was passed by the European Union (EU) in 2016 to protect the privacy and personal data of individuals within the EU.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/general.title: General agents
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/general.description: General agents (GAs) are individuals or organizations that act as intermediaries between insurance companies and insurance agents or brokers.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/geograp.title: Geographic Differential
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/geograp.description: Geographic differential refers to the difference in pay or compensation based on the location of the job or employee, accounting for variations in cost of living, taxes, and other factors.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gender-.title: Gender pay gap
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gender-.description: The gender pay gap is between men’s and women’s average earnings. This can be measured in various ways, but a standard measure is the ratio of women’s median earnings to men’s.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gender-.title: Gender Wage Gap
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gender-.description: The gender wage gap, also known as the gender pay gap, refers to the difference in the average earnings of men and women.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/genetic.title: Genetic-Based Discrimination
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/genetic.description: Genetic-based discrimination refers to the unfair treatment of individuals based on their genetic makeup, particularly in regards to inherited diseases or risk of developing them.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/generat.title: Generation Z
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/generat.description: Generation Z, born mid-1990s to mid-2010s, is tech-savvy, politically aware, diverse, and open to mental health discussions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gender-.title: Gender Identity
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gender-.description: Gender identity is a person’s internal sense of their own gender. It refers to how a person identifies themselves in terms of their gender and can be different from the sex they were assigned at birth.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gender-.title: Gender Expression
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gender-.description: Gender expression refers to the ways in which a person expresses their gender identity through their appearance, behavior, and mannerisms.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/equal-e.title: Equal Employment Opportunity
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/equal-e.description: Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) is a set of laws, policies, and guidelines prohibiting workplace discrimination based on specific protected characteristics.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/environ.title: Environmental Scan
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/environ.description: What is an environmental scan? An environmental scan is the process of monitoring, analyzing, and gathering information about the external factors that may impact an organization. It is a process of gathering and interpreting information about an organization’s internal and external environment. It encompasses assessing the economic, political, social, technological, and legal factors that could…

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gender-.title: Gender Divide
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gender-.description: The gender divide in the workforce refers to the differences in opportunities, rights, and privileges between men and women in terms of employment, pay, and representation in different profession.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/environ.title: Environment Scanning
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/environ.description: Environment scanning, also known as external scanning or situation analysis, is the process of monitoring, analyzing, and gathering information about the external factors that may impact an organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/enterpr.title: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/enterpr.description: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) is a software system that helps organizations manage and automate various business processes such as accounting, inventory management, human resources, procurement, and customer relationship management.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/what-is.title: Gamification
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/what-is.description: Gamification is the process of using game design elements to make non-game activities more engaging and motivating for users.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/enterpr.title: Enterprise compensation management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/enterpr.description: Enterprise compensation management aims to create a fair and competitive compensation system that aligns with the organization’s overall business strategy and attracts, motivates, and retains the best employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gag-cla.title: Gag Clause
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/gag-cla.description: A Gag clause is a provision in an agreement that prohibits one or more parties from making any negative or critical statements about the other party.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/encore-.title: Encore Career
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/encore-.description: An encore career is a term used to describe a career change that takes place later in an individual’s working life, typically after age 50.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/empower.title: Empowerment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/empower.description: Empowerment is the process of giving individuals or groups the ability to make choices and take control of their own lives.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employm.title: Employment Rate
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employm.description: The employment rate is a measure of the percentage of the working-age population that is currently employed. It is often used as an indicator of the health of the labor market and the overall economy.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/furloug.title: Furlough
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/furloug.description: A temporary leave of absence for employees typically taken when an employer cannot fully pay its staff, with the expectation that employees will return to work later.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/fully-i.title: Fully Insured Plan
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/fully-i.description: A Fully Insured Plan is a type of health insurance plan in which the employer pays a premium to the insurance company, who assumes the financial risk for claims.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/full-ti.title: Full time Equivalent (FTE)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/full-ti.description: Full-time Equivalent (FTE) is a measure used to calculate the number of full-time employees that a company has based on the total number of hours worked.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/freemiu.title: Freemium
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/freemiu.description: Freemium is a business model where a product or service is offered for free but with the option to pay for additional features or benefits. It is used to attract a large number of users and convert some of them into paying customers.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/freedom.title: Freedom of Association
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/freedom.description: Freedom of Association refers to the right to come together with other individuals to collectively express, promote, pursue, and defend common interests, and includes the right to form and join trade unions, political parties, and social clubs.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/fraud-t.title: Fraud Triangle
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/fraud-t.description: The Fraud Triangle consists of pressure, opportunity and rationalization, which together create conditions for committing fraud. It results in financial loss, reputation damage, legal consequences, personal consequences and decrease in public trust.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/form-i-.title: Form I-9 or I-9 Form
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/form-i-.description: Form I-9, also known as the Employment Eligibility Verification Form, is used by U.S employers to verify the identity and employment eligibility of individuals hired for employment in the United States, it’s mandatory, protects from penalties and helps to maintain a legal workforce.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/form-12.title: Form 12B
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/form-12.description: Form 12B is a statement of TDS on salary income used in India, it contains information such as employer and employee details, TDS deducted and deposited, used for compliance, record keeping, credit for TDS paid, transparency, and auditing.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/forecas.title: Forecasting
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/forecas.description: Forecasting is the process of predicting future events or conditions based on historical data, it helps organizations make informed decisions but it’s not always accurate and it can be resource-intensive.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/forced-.title: Forced Ranking
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/forced-.description: Forced Ranking is a performance management system that ranks employees relative to their peers, it can provide objective evaluation but can also lead to unfair evaluations or discourage collaboration and teamwork.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/forced-.title: Forced Distribution
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/forced-.description: Forced Distribution is a performance management technique used to evaluate and rank employees based on their performance, it can provide objective evaluation, but can also lead to unfair evaluations or discourage collaboration and teamwork.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/fly-in-.title: Fly In, Fly Out
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/fly-in-.description: Fly In, Fly Out is a type of work arrangement where employees fly to a remote location for a certain period of time to work, it provides access to a larger pool of skilled workers, but also comes with challenges such as isolation and disruption of personal lives.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/flexibl.title: Flexible Benefits Plan
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/flexibl.description: Flexible-Benefits Plan allows employees to choose from a range of benefits options, it can help attract and retain talent, control costs and adapt to the changing needs of employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/flexibl.title: Flexible Working
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/flexibl.description: Flexible Working is an arrangement that allows employees to work outside traditional office hours or locations, it improves work-life balance, increases productivity and helps retain top talent.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/flexibl.title: Flexible Work Arrangements
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/flexibl.description: Flexible Work Arrangements refers to deviation from traditional 9-5 schedule, providing employees greater flexibility in terms of when, where, and how they work, improving work-life balance, productivity, and employee retention and recruitment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/flexibl.title: Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/flexibl.description: Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) are pre-tax benefit plans that allow employees to set aside money to pay for out-of-pocket health care and dependent care expenses, resulting in significant tax savings and better management of expenses.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/fixed-t.title: Fixed Term Employment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/fixed-t.description: Fixed-term Employment is a type of employment contract where the employee is hired for a specific period of time, with a specific start and end date, for a specific project or task and have limited job security and benefits.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/five-fa.title: Five Factor Model
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/five-fa.description: Five Factor Model (FFM) is a theoretical framework in psychology that describes five broad dimensions of personality, which are Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Neuroticism. It is widely accepted and researched framework for understanding personality.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/feather.title: Featherbedding
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/feather.description: Featherbedding is a practice of requiring employers to hire more workers than necessary to complete a job, in order to provide work for union members, leading to inefficiencies and increased labor costs for employers.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/family-.title: Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/family-.description: The Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) requires employers to provide eligible employees with up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave per year for certain family and medical reasons, such as the birth or adoption of a child, the care of an immediate family member with a serious health condition, and the employee’s own serious health condition.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/fair-re.title: Fair Representation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/fair-re.description: Fair Representation ensures equal opportunity for all individuals or groups to have their interests and perspectives represented in decision-making processes. It promotes democracy, prevent oppression and promote social and economic justice.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/fair-la.title: Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/fair-la.description: The Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) is a federal law that establishes minimum wage, overtime pay, and child labor standards for employers.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/factor-.title: Factor Comparison
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/factor-.description: Factor Comparison is a technique used to evaluate and compare jobs, employees, or candidates based on a set of predefined factors or criteria.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/extrins.title: Extrinsic Reward
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/extrins.description: Extrinsic Reward are external incentives or benefits given to an individual to motivate them to engage in a particular behavior or activity. They can be tangible or intangible, and are often used in conjunction with intrinsic motivation to foster long-term engagement and commitment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/extrins.title: Extrinsic Motivation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/extrins.description: Extrinsic Motivation is driven by external rewards such as money, grades, recognition etc. It can be a powerful force in motivating individuals, but should be used in conjunction with intrinsic motivation to foster long-term engagement and commitment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/expense.title: Expenses
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/expense.description: Expenses are the costs incurred in the course of earning income or providing goods or services, they are important for budgeting, financial planning, taxation, cost control and performance evaluation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/expatri.title: Expatriate
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/expatri.description: Expatriate is a person who temporarily or permanently lives in a country other than their own; sent by their employer for a specific project, assignment or permanently; faces challenges of adjusting to a new culture, language and ways of doing things.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/exempt-.title: Exempt Employee
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/exempt-.description: Exempt Employees are salaried workers who are not entitled to certain labor protections like overtime pay, minimum wage and meal and rest breaks, typically considered as managers, administrators or professional workers.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/executi.title: Executive search: process, firms and guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/executi.description: Executive Search is a recruitment method where a company hires a professional search firm to find and recruit a highly qualified candidate for a specific, senior-level executive position within the company.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employm.title: Employment History
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employm.description: What is employment history? Employment history is typically provided by job candidates on their resumes and is verified by the employer through reference checks and background checks. Employment history is typically provided by job candidates on their resumes and is verified by the employer through reference checks and background checks. It is essential for job…

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employm.description: Employment law compliance is a foundational HR responsibility that protects employees and shields organizations from costly legal liability. What are employment laws? Employment laws and regulations govern the relationship between employers and employees and protect employees from discrimination, mistreatment, and other workplace misconduct. Overall, employment laws are in place to protect employees from mistreatment and…

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employm.title: Employment Branding
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employm.description: What is employment branding? Employment branding creates and promotes an organization’s reputation and perception as an employer of choice. It is a way for organizations to communicate their unique culture, values, and employment experience to potential and current employees and the general public. Employment branding aims to attract and retain top talent and create an…

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employm.title: Employment at will
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employm.description: What is employment at will? Employment at will is a U.S. legal rule allowing employers to fire employees at any time, for any reason (unless illegal), or for no reason, without notice. https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/executi.title: Executive compensation: components and HR guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/executi.description: Executive compensation refers to the compensation packages provided to top executives of a company, including base salary, bonuses, stock options, and other incentives.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/executi.title: Executive coaching: definition, benefits and guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/executi.description: Executive Coaching is a professional development process in which a coach helps leaders and executives to improve their performance, develop leadership skills and achieve their goals, it is done through goal-setting, skill-building, and action planning.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/ex-grat.title: Ex gratia payment: definition, tax and HR guide (2026)
