https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/ex-grat.description: Ex Gratia Payments are voluntary payments made by an employer or organization, usually outside of a legally binding contract, as a gesture of goodwill or to settle a dispute without any admission of liability or fault.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/essenti.title: Essential functions: ADA definition and HR guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/essenti.description: Essential Functions are the fundamental and necessary job duties that an individual must be able to perform in order to be considered qualified for a particular position. They are specific to the job and used in evaluating an individual’s qualifications and abilities.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/due-dil.title: Due diligence in HR: definition and guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/due-dil.description: Due Diligence is the investigation or auditing of a potential investment or product to confirm all facts, such as reviewing financial records and contracts.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/equity-.title: Equity theory: definition, examples and HR guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/equity-.description: Equity Theory is a social psychological theory that explains how individuals perceive and respond to perceived unfairness in social exchanges, it proposes that individuals compare their own efforts and outcomes to others, and adjust their behavior in order to reduce or eliminate feelings of inequity.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/equity/.title: Equity in the workplace
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/equity/.description: Equity refers to fairness and impartiality in the distribution of resources and opportunities. It ensures that everyone has an equal chance to succeed.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee onboarding: process, checklist and guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee onboarding is the process of integrating new employees into an organization, familiarizing them with company culture, policies, and processes, and preparing them for their role.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/dual-la.title: Dual labour markets: definition and HR guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/dual-la.description: Dual Labour Markets refers to the existence of two separate labour markets within an economy; one with good wages, benefits and working conditions, the other with lower wages, fewer benefits and less favorable working conditions, leading to increased inequality and reduced social mobility.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee net promoter score (eNPS): guide (2026)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee Net Promoter Score (ENPS) is a metric measuring employee engagement and satisfaction via a simple survey.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/dual-ca.title: Dual Career Ladder/Track
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/dual-ca.description: Dual Career Ladder/Track is a type of employment structure where employees have opportunities to advance in two separate but related career paths, providing flexibility, career development and retention while increasing productivity, but also requiring employees to balance multiple roles and responsibilities.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Management Software
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee management software is a tool that automates and streamlines HR processes such as recruitment, onboarding, performance, compliance, and time tracking to improve the employee life cycle and company culture.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Lifecycle
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: The Employee Lifecycle is a model for managing the different stages of an employee’s time with an organization, from recruitment to retirement, with the goal of improving engagement.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Handbook
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: An Employee Handbook is a document outlining company policies, procedures, and expectations for employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Experience
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee Experience is the overall perception and attitudes of employees towards their workplace and employment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Expense Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee Expense Management is the process of tracking, approving, and reimbursing employee-incurred business expenses.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Exit Survey
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee Exit Survey is a survey given to employees leaving a company to gather feedback about their experience working there.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/draw/.title: Draw
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/draw/.description: Draw refers to a situation where a game or competition ends with no winner or loser, or in an organization, where there is no clear winner or loser in a decision-making process, requires tie-breaking or compromise to resolve the outcome.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/downsiz.title: Downsizing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/downsiz.description: Downsizing refers to the process of reducing the size of a company, organization or workforce.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Engagement Program
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee engagement program is a set of initiatives and activities aimed at improving overall engagement, motivation, and satisfaction of employees within an organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/downshi.title: Downshifting
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/downshi.description: Downshifting refers to a lifestyle choice where an individual reduces their work hours, income, or status to pursue other activities, achieve a better work-life balance and increased fulfillment in their personal and professional life.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/domesti.title: Domestic Inquiry
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/domesti.description: A Domestic Inquiry is a formal investigation into alleged misconduct or violation of company rules by an employee, conducted by an impartial party with evidence-based findings and due process rights for the employee.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employer Branding
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employer branding creates and manages an organization’s reputation and perception as an employer. It is how an organization positions itself as an employer of choice and is closely linked to its overall branding and reputation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employer brand
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: An employer brand is the reputation and perception of an organization as an employer. It is how an organization is perceived by current and potential employees and is closely linked to its overall brand and reputation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee-Driven Idea System
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: An employee-driven idea system is a system or process where employees are encouraged to share their ideas and suggestions for improving the organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/domesti.title: Domestic HRM
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/domesti.description: Domestic HRM manages human resources within a single country, including recruiting, hiring, training, and managing employees, as well as compliance with national labor laws.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employer Value proposition
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: An Employer Value Proposition (EVP) is a statement that describes the unique value and benefits that an organization offers to its employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Value Proposition (EVP)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: An Employee Value Proposition (EVP) is a statement that describes the unique benefits and opportunities that an organization offers to its employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Empowerment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee empowerment is the process of giving employees the authority, autonomy and resources to make decisions and take ownership of their work.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/diversi.title: Diversity Training
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/diversi.description: Diversity Training educates and increases awareness on issues of diversity, inclusion, and cultural competence for creating inclusive workplaces.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Onboarding Software
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee Onboarding Software streamlines and automates the process of introducing new hires to the company, improving efficiency, retention, and personalization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/diversi.title: Diversity and Inclusion (D&I)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/diversi.description: Diversity and Inclusion are key to fostering a culture of innovation, creativity, and growth. Embracing differences allows for unique perspectives and ideas.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Onboarding Surveys
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee Onboarding Surveys gather feedback to improve onboarding and employee engagement.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Turnover
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee turnover refers to the rate at which employees leave an organization and are replaced by new hires.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Silence
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee silence is when employees choose not to speak up or share their thoughts, ideas, or concerns about their work environment, even when they may have important feedback to offer.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Orientation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee orientation is the process of introducing new hires to the company and its culture, policies, procedures, and expectations to ensure a positive transition.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Self-Service Portal
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: n Employee Self-Service (ESS) portal is a web-based platform that allows employees to access and manage their personal and employment-related information.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Recruitment Software
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee recruitment software automates and streamlines the hiring process, improves organization and candidate experience, increases reach and compliance, and saves time and money.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Referral Program
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee Referral Program is a recruitment strategy where current employees refer job candidates to the company.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employees Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI) is life insurance provided by EPFO for private sector employees with an employer-paid premium based on EPF coverage.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Database
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: An Employee Database is a system that stores and organizes employee information for easy access, management, and compliance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Clearance
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee clearance is a process of verifying and documenting that an individual is suitable and eligible to access certain information or facilities within a company or organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Self Service (ESS)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee Self Service (ESS) is a system that allows employees to access, view, and manage their personal and employment-related information.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Benefits
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee benefits are non-wage compensation offered by employers to attract and retain employees, such as health insurance, retirement plans, paid time off, disability insurance, and life insurance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee scheduling software
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee scheduling software allows managers and supervisors to create and manage their employees’ schedules and includes features such as shift assignments, time off requests, and schedule conflict resolution.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Satisfaction
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee satisfaction refers to the level of contentment and fulfillment that employees feel in their work and with their organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee assistance program (EAP)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: An Employee Assistance Program (EAP) is a confidential, short-term counseling and referral service provided to employees and their family members by an employer to address personal and work-related problems.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Retention
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee retention refers to the ability of an organization to keep its employees over time. It measures the stability and continuity of an organization’s workforce and is used as an indicator.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Advocacy
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee advocacy is the act of promoting the interests and well-being of employees within a company.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Resource Groups (ERGs)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) are employees who share a common identity or interest, such as race, gender, sexual orientation, or veteran status.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: An employee is a person who is hired by an organization to perform specific job duties and tasks, typically in exchange for a salary or wages and benefits.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.title: Employee Relations (ER)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employe.description: Employee relations (ER) refers to the relationship between an organization and its employees. The goal of ER is to create a positive and productive work environment for employees while also ensuring that the organization’s needs and objectives are met.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/emotion.title: Emotional Intelligence
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/emotion.description: Emotional intelligence (EI) refers to the ability to understand and manage one’s own emotions and the emotions of others.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/eeo-1-s.title: EEO-1 Survey
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/eeo-1-s.description: The EEO-1 survey is a form that certain employers file with the EEOC to provide data on their employees’ race, ethnicity, and gender to identify patterns of discrimination.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/eeo-1-r.title: EEO-1 Report
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/eeo-1-r.description: The EEO-1 Report is a form that certain employers file with the EEOC to provide data on their employees’ race, ethnicity, and gender, to identify patterns of discrimination.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/early-r.title: Early Return to Work program (also, graduated return to work)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/early-r.description: A program to safely return employees to work after absence due to illness or injury.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/e-recru.title: E-Recruitment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/e-recru.description: E-recruitment is the use of web-based technology to identify, screen, and hire job candidates, offering cost and time-saving benefits but also some limitations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/e-learn.title: E-learning
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/e-learn.description: E-learning refers to the use of technology to deliver training programs to employees, allowing for cost-effective and convenient learning.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/diversi.title: Diversity
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/diversi.description: Diversity encompasses differences in characteristics such as race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, and more; fostering inclusiveness, multidimensionality, and respect, resulting in increased innovation and better decision making.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/distrib.title: Distributive Bargaining
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/distrib.description: Distributive Bargaining, also known as “competitive” or “zero-sum” bargaining, is a negotiation strategy where parties aim to maximize their own outcomes while minimizing the other party’s outcomes, by using pressure and concessions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/distanc.title: Distance Learning
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/distanc.description: Distance Learning refers to a method of education where students learn remotely through online materials, with little or no face-to-face interaction. It offers flexibility and accessibility but with limited interaction and potential technical difficulties.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/dispara.title: Disparate Treatment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/dispara.description: Disparate Treatment refers to discrimination where an individual or group is treated less favorably based on a protected characteristic, recognized as a claim under federal civil rights laws in US.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/dispara.title: Disparate Impact
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/dispara.description: Disparate Impact refers to policies or practices that disproportionately affect certain protected groups negatively, recognized as a claim under Civil Rights Act of 1964 in US.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/disease.title: Disease Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/disease.description: Disease Management is a systematic approach to improving health and quality of life of individuals with chronic conditions by coordinating care, supporting self-management and using evidence-based guidelines and interventions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/discrim.title: Discrimination
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/discrim.description: Discrimination refers to the unjust or prejudicial treatment of individuals or groups on the basis of certain characteristics, such as race, gender, age, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or national origin.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/demotio.title: Demotion
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/demotio.description: A demotion is an act of moving an employee to a lower position or rank within the company.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/discret.title: Discretionary Bonus
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/discret.description: A Discretionary Bonus is a bonus awarded at the discretion of an employer or supervisor, typically not guaranteed and may be awarded based on factors such as an employee’s performance, company’s financial performance or achievement of specific goals.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/what-is.title: Delayering
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/what-is.description: Delayering is the process of reducing the number of layers in an organizational hierarchy, for the purpose of improving communication, reducing costs, increasing flexibility, and improving employee motivation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/discipl.title: Disciplinary Procedure
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/discipl.description: Disciplinary Procedure is a process used by an organization to address alleged violations of rules or policies by employees or members, ensuring a safe and productive work environment and maintaining the integrity of the organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/defined.title: Defined Contribution
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/defined.description: Defined contribution is a retirement plan where employer or employee contribute to individual account, employee bears investment risk, benefit based on contributions and returns.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/defined.title: Defined Benefit Plan
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/defined.description: A defined-benefit plan is a type of retirement plan in which employer guarantees a certain benefit to employee at retirement, based on factors such as salary and length of service.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/discipl.title: Disciplinary Action
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/discipl.description: Disciplinary Action refers to measures taken to correct or punish employee behavior that violates company policies or expectations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/deferre.title: Deferred Compensation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/deferre.description: Deferred compensation is an employment benefit where salary is received later with tax deferral advantage.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/deep-le.title: Deep learning
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/deep-le.description: Deep learning is a type of machine learning that uses neural networks to learn from data, improve automatically and make decisions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/dead-en.title: Dead end Job
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/dead-en.description: A dead-end job is a position with little potential for career advancement or growth.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/de-mini.title: De Minimis Rule
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/de-mini.description: Learn about the de minimis rule: its meaning, benefits, and drawbacks. Understand how ignoring small sums can impact transparency, tax purposes, and overall performance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/data-br.title: Data Breach
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/data-br.description: A data breach is an incident where sensitive information is accessed, viewed, stolen, or used by an unauthorized individual or entity.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/customi.title: Customised Employment (CE)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/customi.description: Customized Employment (CE) is a process used to match people with disabilities with job that is tailored to their unique strengths, interests, and abilities.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/curricu.title: Curriculum Vitae
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/curricu.description: A Curriculum Vitae (CV) is a comprehensive document that lists a person’s educational and professional qualifications, often used for academic or research positions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/crowdso.title: Crowdsourcing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/crowdso.description: Obtaining services, ideas or content by soliciting contributions from a large group of people, often through online platforms.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/disabil.title: Disability Income Insurance
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/disabil.description: Disability Income Insurance is a type of insurance that provides financial protection to individuals unable to work due to disability, by replacing a portion of their income.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/disabil.title: Disability
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/disabil.description: Disability refers to a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities, protected under American with Disabilities Act (ADA) in terms of employment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cross-t.title: Cross-Training Employees
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cross-t.description: Cross-training is the process of training employees to perform multiple tasks and functions, improving organizational efficiency, employee engagement, adaptability and continuity.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/direct-.title: Direct Threat
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/direct-.description: Direct Threat refers to a significant risk of substantial harm to the health or safety of others that cannot be eliminated or reduced, posed by an employee with a disability.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/direct-.title: Direct Marketing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/direct-.description: Direct Marketing is an advertising method that allows businesses to communicate directly with customers through targeted campaigns, with measurable results and personalization, typically through channels like mail, email, telephone, and text message.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cross-f.title: Cross-Functional Team
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cross-f.description: Cross-functional teams are groups of individuals from different functional areas that work together to achieve a common goal, bringing diverse perspectives, skills, and resources.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/develop.title: Developmental Counselling
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/develop.description: Developmental Counseling helps individuals identify, set and achieve personal growth goals while improving self-awareness and overcoming obstacles.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/deregul.title: Deregulation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/deregul.description: Deregulation is the process of removing or reducing government regulations and restrictions on businesses, with the aim of promoting economic growth and efficiency.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/counter.title: Counterproductive Work Behaviours (CWB)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/counter.description: Counterproductive Work Behaviors (CWB) refer to actions or attitudes by employees that harm the organization or its members.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/depende.title: Dependent Care Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/depende.description: Dependent Care Flexible Spending Account (FSA) is an employer-sponsored benefit that allows employees to set aside pre-tax money for dependent care expenses and provides tax savings, cost savings on dependent care expenses and flexibility.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/departm.title: DOL / BOLI
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/departm.description: DOL enforces 180+ federal labor laws; BOLI is Oregon’s state agency. See WHD, OSHA, OFCCP, EBSA, Oregon civil rights, and HR compliance map.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cost-pe.title: Cost Per Hire
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cost-pe.description: Cost per hire is total recruiting cost divided by hires. See SHRM/ANSI formula, 2026 $4,700 benchmark, hidden vacancy cost, and reduction playbook.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cost-be.title: Cost-Benefit Analysis
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cost-be.description: Cost-benefit analysis weighs project costs against benefits. See NPV / BCR / IRR formulas, HR investment ROI examples, and step-by-step framework.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cost-to.title: Cost to Company (CTC)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cost-to.description: CTC is total annual employer spend per employee. See CTC vs gross vs net salary, India structure (Basic, HRA, EPF), and offer-letter navigation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cost-pe.title: Cost Per Impression
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cost-pe.description: CPM measures ad cost per 1,000 impressions. See formula, CPM vs CPC vs CPA, recruitment marketing benchmarks, LinkedIn / Indeed rates, and viewability.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/corpora.title: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/corpora.description: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is a company’s voluntary actions to improve social and environmental well-being, beyond legal obligations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/corpora.title: Corporate Personhood
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/corpora.description: Corporate Personhood is the legal concept that recognizes corporations as separate legal entities with rights similar to natural persons.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compete.title: Competencies
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compete.description: Core competencies are the unique strengths and abilities of a company that give it a competitive advantage in the market.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/coopera.title: Cooperative
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/coopera.description: A cooperative is a business organization owned and operated by its members for mutual benefit, providing goods or services while distributing profits among members.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/convers.title: Conversion Rate
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/convers.description: A conversion rate is a metric that expresses the percentage of visitors who take a desired action on a website or landing page.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/contrac.title: Contract of Service
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/contrac.description: A contract of service is a legal agreement between an employer and employee outlining the terms and conditions of the employment relationship.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/conting.title: Contingent Worker
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/conting.description: A contingent worker is an individual hired on a non-permanent basis, typically for a specific project or assignment, rather than an ongoing role with a company.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/conting.title: Contingent Staff
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/conting.description: Contingent staff refers to employees who are not on a permanent contract and are typically hired on a temporary, project or seasonal basis.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/conting.title: Contingency Recruiter
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/conting.description: Contingency Recruiters are professionals who identify, screen and recruit candidates for job openings on a contingency basis, only paid for successful placement, flexible and cost-effective, but with no guarantee of success and lack of control over process.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/conting.title: Contingency Approach
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/conting.description: Contingency Approach is a management strategy that adapts decision-making and problem-solving based on the specific context of a situation, allowing for flexibility, problem-solving and improved organizational performance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/consult.title: Consultant
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/consult.description: Consultants are experts who provide advice, guidance, and expertise to organizations to help them improve their performance, operations, or achieve specific goals, they work independently or as part of a consulting firm and have diverse areas of expertise.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/constru.title: Constructive Discharge
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/constru.description: Constructive Discharge refers to a situation where an employee is forced to quit their job due to the employer’s intentional and severe actions, creating unbearable working conditions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/conflic.title: Conflict of Interest
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/conflic.description: Conflict of Interest refers to a situation where an individual or organization’s personal, financial, or other interests may compromise their ability to make objective decisions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/conflic.title: Conflict Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/conflic.description: Conflict Management is a process of addressing and resolving disputes, using techniques like active listening, empathy, identification of common goals, brainstorming and negotiation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/confirm.title: Confirmation Letter
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/confirm.description: Confirmation Letters serve to formally verify the details of an agreement, such as job offers, reservations, interviews, events, payments, deliveries, and appointments.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/configu.title: Configurability
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/configu.description: Configurability refers to the ability of a system or product to be customized or tailored to meet specific needs and adjust to changing requirements.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/confide.title: Confidentiality Agreement
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/confide.description: A Confidentiality Agreement is a legally binding contract between two or more parties in which one or more parties agree to not disclose certain confidential information to third parties.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/confere.title: Conference Calls
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/confere.description: Conference Calls are a way for people to communicate remotely by connecting over the phone or internet, audio and video options available, useful for presentations, collaboration and building relationships.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/complia.title: Compliance
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/complia.description: Compliance refers to the adherence to laws, regulations, standards and policies, it helps mitigate risk, build trust, avoid penalties and gain competitive advantage.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/competi.title: Competitive Advantage
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/competi.description: Competitive Advantage is the unique advantage a company has over its competitors, allowing it to generate greater sales or margins.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compete.title: Competency based Training
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compete.description: Competency-based Training (CBT) is a tailored, practical and self-directed method of learning aligned to job roles and organizational goals, it’s cost-effective.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compete.title: Competency Based Pay
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compete.description: Competency-based Pay links employee pay to specific skills, knowledge, and abilities, aligns employee skills with organizational goals, and rewards employees for their demonstrated competencies.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compete.title: Competency Modelling
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compete.description: Competency Modelling is the process of identifying and describing specific abilities, knowledge, skills, and attitudes required for job performance, aligning employee skills with organizational goals.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compete.title: Competences
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compete.description: Competence refers to the skills, knowledge, and attitudes that enable individuals to perform effectively in a specific job or role and can be developed, measured, and used for recruitment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compens.title: Compensatory Time Off (Comp Time)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compens.description: Compensatory Time Off (comp time) is a paid time off earned by employees working overtime, given as an alternative to pay overtime, and regulated by federal labor laws.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compens.title: Compensation
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compens.description: Compensation is the package of rewards offered by an employer including base salary, benefits, bonuses, incentives, and other perks, aimed at attracting, retaining, and motivating employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compass.title: Compassion Fatigue
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compass.description: Compassion Fatigue is a condition that can occur in those who work in helping professions, it is characterized by emotional exhaustion, detachment, difficulty caring, burnout, negative self-concept and physical symptoms. It can lead to burnout and negatively impact personal and professional life.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compara.title: Comparable Worth
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compara.description: Comparable Worth is the idea that the value of different jobs should be determined based on the skills and responsibilities required, rather than on societal biases and market forces.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compa-r.title: Compa ratio
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compa-r.description: Compa-ratio is a ratio used to compare an employee’s salary to the market value of their job, expressed as a percentage.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/common-.title: Common law Employee
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/common-.description: A Common-law Employee is a worker hired on an “at-will” basis to perform a specific job or task, with the employer having the right to control the work.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sales-c.title: Sales Commission
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/sales-c.description: Sales commission is variable pay tied to sales results. See 8 structures, OTE 50/50 split, SaaS rates 8-12%, accelerators, and plan design playbook.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/commiss.title: Commission
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/commiss.description: Commission is variable pay tied to specific transactions or revenue. See types, FLSA / minimum wage, tax treatment, vs bonus, and design playbook.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/collect.title: Collective Bargaining
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/collect.description: Collective bargaining is union-employer negotiation. See NLRA, mandatory subjects, the bargaining process, CBA structure, and good-faith duty.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cogniti.title: Cognitive Computing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cogniti.description: Cognitive computing simulates human thought process. See IBM Watson origin, vs AI, NLP / ML / expert systems, HR use cases, and 2026 LLM evolution.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cogniti.title: Cognitive Ability Test
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cogniti.description: A cognitive ability test measures GMA — the strongest single hiring predictor. See Schmidt-Hunter validity, EEOC adverse impact, and types.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/code-of.title: Code of Practice
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/code-of.description: A code of practice is statutory or industry guidance from a regulator. See UK ACAS codes, 25% tribunal uplift, and code of practice vs conduct vs ethics.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/code-of.title: Code of Ethics
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/code-of.description: A code of ethics states an organisation’s underlying values and principles. See vs code of conduct, examples (ICF, AMA), SOX 406, and structure.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/code-of.title: Code of Conduct
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/code-of.description: A code of conduct is the rules employees must follow at work. See structure, vs code of ethics, enforcement, SOX 406 requirements, and template.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/coachin.title: Coaching
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/coachin.description: Workplace coaching builds capability through structured 1:1 development. See exec / career / team / manager coaching, ICF vs EMCC, ROI, and selection.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/co-empl.title: Co-Employment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/co-empl.description: Co-employment is a shared employer relationship. See PEO vs joint employer, FLSA NLRB tests, Microsoft Vizcaino case, and risk mitigation playbook.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cloud-c.title: Cloud Computing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cloud-c.description: Cloud computing delivers IT resources via the internet. See IaaS/PaaS/SaaS, public/private/hybrid, AWS/Azure/GCP, HR use cases, and security risks.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cloud-b.title: Cloud-Based HR Software
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cloud-b.description: Cloud-based HR software (HRIS / HCM) runs in the cloud rather than on-premise. See Workday, SAP, Rippling, BambooHR, AI shift, and selection guide.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/climate.title: Climate Surveys
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/climate.description: A climate survey measures the perceived workplace environment. See climate vs engagement vs culture, key dimensions, questions, and design playbook.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cipd/.title: CIPD
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cipd/.description: The CIPD is the UK’s chartered professional body for HR & L&D. See levels 3/5/7, Foundation/Associate/Chartered membership, salary impact, value.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/churn-r.title: Churn Rate
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/churn-r.description: Employee churn rate is the % of staff leaving over a period. See formula, churn vs turnover vs attrition, industry benchmarks, and reduction playbook.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/chief-t.title: Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/chief-t.description: The CTO leads product engineering, innovation, and technical strategy. See CTO vs CIO, startup vs enterprise CTO archetypes, salary, and 2026 trends.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/chief-i.title: Chief Information Officer (CIO)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/chief-i.description: The CIO leads enterprise IT, security, and data. See CIO vs CTO vs CDO, responsibilities, AI impact, salary, and the modern CIO 2026 mandate.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/chief-e.title: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/chief-e.description: The CEO is the highest-ranking executive accountable to the board. See responsibilities, reporting structure, US vs UK chairman split, and CEO pay.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/chatbot.title: Chatbots
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/chatbot.description: HR chatbots automate recruiting, onboarding, employee Q&A. See use cases, ROI, NYC LL144 / EU AI Act compliance, agentic AI shift, and selection guide.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/charism.title: Charismatic Authority
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/charism.description: Charismatic authority is leadership through personal magnetism, from Max Weber. See Weber’s 3 types, examples, succession problem, and dark-side risks.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/change-.title: Change Programme
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/change-.description: A change programme coordinates multiple projects to deliver transformation. See MSP framework, programme vs project, benefits realisation, and HR role.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/change-.title: Change Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/change-.description: Change management helps people adopt new ways of working. See Kotter 8-step, Prosci ADKAR, Lewin, Kubler-Ross, ACMP Standard, and 2026 AI trends.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/catfish.title: Catfish Effect
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/catfish.description: The catfish effect uses a stronger competitor to motivate weaker performers. See Norway origin, Haier example, HR applications, and risks.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/casual-.title: Casual Employment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/casual-.description: Casual employment has no firm advance commitment. See Australia’s Aug 2024 Fair Work changes, employee choice pathway, US/UK equivalents, and risks.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/carve-o.title: Carve-Out
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/carve-o.description: A carve-out separates a business unit from its parent for sale or independence. See HR playbook, TSAs, stranded costs, retention, and EIN setup.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/carrier.title: Carrier
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/carrier.description: A Carrier is a person or company that transports goods or people from one place to another, typically by air, water, or land.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/career-.title: Career plateau
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/career-.description: A Career Plateau is a point in a person’s career where they reach a level of stability and their career progress slows or stops.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/career-.title: Career path
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/career-.description: A Career Path is the trajectory of a person’s career, and can involve following a specific progression within a particular industry or field.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/career-.title: Career development
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/career-.description: Career Development is the process of managing your own learning, career, and work, and involves setting goals, learning new skills, and gaining new experiences.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/career-.title: Career break
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/career-.description: A Career Break is a temporary interruption of one’s professional life, typically for personal reasons such as travel, family responsibilities, or self-improvement.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/capitat.title: Capitated pricing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/capitat.description: Capitated Pricing is a payment model in which a healthcare provider is paid a fixed amount per patient, regardless of the number or type of services provided.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/capabil.title: Capability assessment tools
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/capabil.description: Capability Assessment Tools are used to evaluate an individual’s skills and abilities in a specific area. They can be helpful in identifying strengths and weaknesses and setting development goals.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/candida.title: Candidate relationship management (CRM)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/candida.description: Candidate Relationship Marketing (CRM) is a recruiting strategy that involves building long-term relationships with potential candidates and creating a pool of qualified and interested candidates for future job opportunities.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/candida.title: Candidate experience
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/candida.description: Candidate Experience refers to the perception that job candidates have of an organization during the recruiting and hiring process.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cafeter.title: Cafeteria plan
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/cafeter.description: A cafeteria plan (Section 125) lets employees pick pre-tax benefits from a flexible menu. Learn eligibility, FSA/HSA/HRA options, compliance rules and setup steps for enterprise HR teams.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/byod-br.title: BYOD (bring your own device)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/byod-br.description: BYOD lets employees use personal devices for work. Learn how to build a compliant BYOD policy covering GDPR, SOC2, MDM, and enterprise HR best practices.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/buzz-ma.title: Buzz marketing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/buzz-ma.description: Buzz marketing in HR turns employees into brand advocates, driving word-of-mouth for employer branding and talent acquisition. Enterprise HR teams guide.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/butterf.title: Butterfly effect
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/butterf.description: The butterfly effect in HR shows how one hiring decision, policy change, or manager behavior cascades into major organizational outcomes. Workplace examples and HR strategy.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/busines.title: Business process outsourcing (BPO)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/busines.description: Business process outsourcing (BPO) lets enterprises delegate HR, payroll and compliance to specialist vendors. Learn types, risks and how to evaluate vendors.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/busines.title: Business necessity
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/busines.description: Business necessity is the EEOC legal standard requiring employers to prove a selection criterion or employment practice is directly job-related and essential to safe, efficient business operation. Enterprise HR compliance guide.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/busines.title: Business Ethics
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/busines.description: Business ethics refers to the principles and values that guide the behavior of individuals and organizations in the business world, including issues such as honesty, fairness, and responsibility.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/busines.title: Business Continuity Planning
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/busines.description: Business Continuity Planning involves creating a system to prevent and recover from potential threats to a company, ensuring it can continue to operate during a disaster.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/busines.title: Business Agility
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/busines.description: Business Agility is the ability to quickly and easily adapt to changes in the market, customer needs, and other internal and external factors, allowing a business to respond to opportunities.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/busines.title: Business
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/busines.description: Business involves the production, distribution, and exchange of goods and services to make a profit. Types include sole proprietorships, partnerships, corporations, and cooperatives.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/burnout.title: Burnout
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/burnout.description: Burnout is a state of physical, emotional, and mental exhaustion caused by excessive and prolonged stress, and can have serious negative consequences for both the individual and the organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bureauc.title: Bureaucratic Inertia
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bureauc.description: Bureaucratic Inertia refers to the tendency of bureaucratic organizations to resist change and maintain the status quo, which can be caused by complex rules, procedures, and hierarchies.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bumping.title: Bumping Rights
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bumping.description: Bumping Rights are often included in collective bargaining agreements between unions and employers and can vary depending on the specific terms of the agreement.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bullyin.title: Bullying
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bullyin.description: Bullying is the use of force or intimidation to abuse or aggressively dominate others. It can take many forms and can have serious short-term and long-term effects on those targeted.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/buddy-s.title: Buddy System
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/buddy-s.description: A Buddy System is a safety or support system in which individuals are paired with a “buddy” who can offer assistance or guidance in a particular situation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/brown-b.title: Brown Bag Lunch
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/brown-b.description: A Brown Bag Lunch is an informal gathering or meeting where attendees bring their own lunch to eat during the event.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/broker/.title: Broker
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/broker/.description: A Broker is a person or firm that acts as an intermediary between buyers and sellers in a financial market or in the sale of goods or services.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/broadba.title: Broadbanding
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/broadba.description: Broadbanding is a type of salary structure that groups jobs into a small number of salary ranges, rather than having a separate pay grade for each job.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/brinkma.title: Brinkmanship
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/brinkma.description: Brinkmanship is the use of provocative or risky actions to push a situation to the brink of conflict, hoping that the other side will back down and make concessions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/brandin.title: Branding
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/brandin.description: Branding refers to the marketing practice of creating a unique name, symbol, or design that identifies and differentiates a product or service from those of other producers.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/brain-d.title: Brain Drain
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/brain-d.description: Brain Drain is the emigration of highly skilled or talented individuals from one country to another, typically from developing countries to developed countries.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bradfor.title: Bradford Factor
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bradfor.description: The Bradford Factor is a tool organization uses to measure the impact of absenteeism on the workplace. Organizations use the Bradford Factor to address absenteeism patterns among their employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/boundar.title: Boundaryless Organization
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/boundar.description: A Boundaryless organization is a type of organization that seeks to break down the barriers between different parts of the company, as well as between the organization and external stakeholders.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/boreout.title: Boreout
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/boreout.description: Boreout is a syndrome characterized by boredom and lack of motivation at work, often caused by a lack of challenging or interesting tasks.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bonus/.title: Bonus
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bonus/.description: A Bonus is an extra payment, benefit, or reward given to an employee or other worker in addition to their regular wages or salary.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bona-fi.title: Bona Fide Occupational Qualification (BFOQ)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bona-fi.description: Bona Fide Occupational Qualification (BFOQ) is a legal concept that allows an employer to make employment decisions based on an individual’s religion, sex, or national origin.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/blue-co.title: Blue-Collar Worker
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/blue-co.description: A blue-collar worker is a worker who performs manual labor, typically in an industrial or manufacturing setting, and may work in industries such as construction, manufacturing, transportation, and utilities.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/blog/.title: Blog
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/blog/.description: Blogs can cover a wide range of topics and are typically written in a more informal or personal style than traditional news articles or academic papers.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/blind-j.title: Blind Job Advert
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/blind-j.description: A blind job advert removes the employer’s identity from a posting to reduce bias and attract diverse candidates. See use cases, legal risks and best practices.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/blind-e.title: Blind Engagement
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/blind-e.description: Blind engagement refers to the act of engaging with someone or something without considering the context or potential consequences.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/blended.title: Blended Workforce
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/blended.description: A blended workforce is a group of employees that includes both traditional employees who work full-time in an office and non-traditional employees who work remotely or on a flexible schedule.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/blackli.title: Blacklisting (Employment)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/blackli.description: Blacklisting is the practice of identifying and publicly naming individuals or organizations that are deemed undesirable or untrustworthy.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/big-fiv.title: Big Five Personality Traits
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/big-fiv.description: The Big Five Personality Traits are five broad dimensions of personality that are used to describe human personality. They are openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/big-dat.title: Big Data in HR
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/big-dat.description: Big data refers to large and complex datasets that are difficult to process using traditional data processing techniques. These datasets are characterized by high volume, high velocity, and high variety.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/best-pr.title: Best Practice Policy
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/best-pr.description: Best Practice Policies are guidelines and recommendations that are considered to be the most effective and efficient ways of achieving a particular goal or objective.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/accessi.title: Accessibility
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/accessi.description: Accessibility is the practice of designing products, devices, services, or environments to be usable by people with disabilities and to enable their full participation in all aspects of life.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/absolut.title: Absolute Rating
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/absolut.description: Absolute ratings are used to assess the creditworthiness of a borrower at a specific point in time based on a detailed analysis of their financial history.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/ally/.title: Ally
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/ally/.description: An ally is a person who actively supports and stands up for the rights and interests of a group other than their own.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/baby-bo.title: Baby Boomers
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/baby-bo.description: Baby boomers are people who were born between 1946 and 1964, during a period of increased birth rates following World War II.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/availab.title: Availability Analysis
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/availab.description: Availability analysis is a method used to assess the reliability and performance of a system, product, or service.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/attenda.title: Attendance Policy
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/attenda.description: An attendance policy is a set of guidelines that outlines the expectations for employee attendance at work. It typically covers issues such as punctuality, absences, tardiness, and notification procedures.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/at-will.title: At-Will Employment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/at-will.description: At-will employment is a type of employment in which either the employee or the employer can terminate the employment relationship at any time, for any reason.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/artific.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in HR
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/artific.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) refers to the ability of a computer or machine to perform tasks that normally require human-like intelligence, such as learning, problem-solving, decision-making, and pattern recognition.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/apprent.title: Apprenticeship
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/apprent.description: An apprenticeship is a formal program of on-the-job training and related classroom instruction that is sponsored by an employer or trade association.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/apprent.title: Apprentice
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/apprent.description: An apprentice is a person who is learning a trade or profession through a formal program of on-the-job training and related classroom instruction.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/allosta.title: Allostatic Load
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/allosta.description: Allostatic load is a measure of the physiological wear and tear on the body that occurs as a result of chronic exposure to stress.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/apprais.title: Appraisal Letter
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/apprais.description: The purpose of an appraisal letter is to provide employees with a clear and detailed summary of their performance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/algorit.title: Algorithmic Transparency
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/algorit.description: Algorithmic transparency refers to the idea that organizations should be transparent about the algorithms and automated decision-making systems that they use.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/apprais.title: Appraisal
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/apprais.description: The purpose of an appraisal is to provide an unbiased and professional assessment of the value of a property or item.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/algorit.title: Algorithmic Accountability
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/algorit.description: Algorithmic accountability refers to the idea that organizations should be held accountable for the algorithms and automated decision-making systems that they use.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/appoint.title: Appointment Schedule
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/appoint.description: An appointment schedule is a schedule that is used to manage appointments or reservations for a service or facility.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/agent-i.title: Agent (Insurance)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/agent-i.description: An insurance agent is a person who represents an insurance company and sells insurance policies to clients. They may work for a single company or represent multiple companies.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/ageism/.title: Ageism
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/ageism/.description: Ageism is prejudice or discrimination against a particular age group, typically older people. It can take many forms, including stereotypes and discriminatory practices.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/age-dis.title: Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/age-dis.description: The Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA) is a federal law that prohibits discrimination against employees who are 40 years of age or older.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/after-a.title: After-Acquired Evidence
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/after-a.description: After-acquired evidence is new evidence that is discovered after a legal decision has been made, which may affect the outcome of the case.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/applica.title: Application Service Provider (ASP)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/applica.description: ASPs are a convenient and cost-effective way for organizations to access and use software applications without having to manage them internally.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/applica.title: Application Form
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/applica.description: The purpose of an application form is to help an employer or HR department gather essential information about a candidate’s qualifications and suitability for a job.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/behavio.title: Behavioral Risk Management
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/behavio.description: Behavioral risk management is the process of identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks that arise from human behavior within an organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/applica.title: Applicant Tracking System (ATS)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/applica.description: ATS is a valuable tool for streamlining and improving the recruitment process. It helps organizations efficiently manage large numbers of job applications and make informed hiring decisions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/what-is.title: Behaviourally Anchored Rating Scale (BARS)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/what-is.description: A Behaviourally anchored Rating Scale (BARS) is a method for evaluating employee performance by comparing their behavior to specific, numerical examples of good performance.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bell-cu.title: Bell Curve
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bell-cu.description: A bell curve is a graphical representation of a normal distribution, which is a symmetrical statistical distribution used to represent and analyze data.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/benchma.title: Benchmarking
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/benchma.description: Benchmarking is the process of comparing the performance of a company or organization with that of other companies or organizations in order to identify best practices and areas for improvement.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/affirma.title: Affirmative Action
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/affirma.description: Affirmative action refers to policies and initiatives that aim to correct for past discrimination and promote diversity and inclusion, often in education and employment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/benefit.title: Benefits Administration
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/benefit.description: Benefits administration is the process of designing, implementing, and managing a company’s employee benefits programs, including health insurance, retirement plans, and other perks.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/affecti.title: Affective Events Theory (AET)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/affecti.description: Affective Events Theory (AET) is a theory that explains how emotions and moods influence work behavior and decision-making.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/benefit.title: Benefits Eligible
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/benefit.description: “Benefits eligible” means an employee meets the requirements to receive certain perks or incentives offered by their employer.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/adverse.title: Adverse Impact
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/adverse.description: Adverse impact refers to a negative or disproportionate effect on a particular group of people, such as a minority group or women.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/adminis.title: Administrative Services Only (ASO)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/adminis.description: Administrative Services Only (ASO) refers to a type of insurance arrangement in which an insurer provides administrative services to a self-insured group, but does not assume any risk for claims.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/benefit.title: Benefits Package
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/benefit.description: A benefits package is a set of perks and incentives, such as health insurance and paid time off, offered by an employer to its employees.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/behavio.title: Behavioral Based Interview
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/behavio.description: Behavioral-based interviews are a type of job interview in which candidates are asked to provide specific examples of their past behavior.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/basic-s.title: Basic salary
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/basic-s.description: Basic salary is a fixed amount of money that an employee is paid on a regular basis, usually on a monthly or biweekly basis.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/adaptiv.title: Adaptive Device
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/adaptiv.description: An adaptive device is a piece of equipment or technology designed to help people with disabilities perform tasks that may otherwise be difficult or impossible.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/applica.title: Applicant
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/applica.description: An applicant is a person who has applied for a job or other opportunities, such as an educational program or a grant.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/basic-c.title: Basic Competencies
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/basic-c.description: Basic competencies are fundamental skills and abilities that are necessary for success in a particular job or role.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/apparen.title: Apparent Authority
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/apparen.description: Apparent authority, also known as “ostensible authority,” is the authority that an individual or organization appears to have based on the actions or statements of another individual or organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/account.title: Accountability
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/account.description: Accountability refers to the obligation to account for one’s actions and accept responsibility for their consequences.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/api-app.title: API (Application Programming Interface)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/api-app.description: An application programming interface (API) is a set of rules and protocols that define how two software systems can interact with each other.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/anti-ne.title: Anti Nepotism Policy
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/anti-ne.description: An anti nepotism policy is a policy that prohibits employees from hiring, promoting, or giving preferential treatment to close personal relationships.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/base-re.title: Base Remuneration
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/base-re.description: Base remuneration is the amount of money that an employee is paid for their work, excluding any bonuses or additional pay.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/absente.title: Absenteeism Policy
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/absente.description: An absenteeism policy is a set of rules and guidelines that outline the acceptable levels of absenteeism in a workplace.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/absente.title: Absenteeism
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/absente.description: Absenteeism is the habit or practice of frequently being absent from work or duty, without good reason.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/base-ra.title: Base Rate
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/base-ra.description: Base rate is a statistical term that refers to the proportion of a population that possesses a certain characteristic or attribute.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/anti-di.title: Anti-Discrimination
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/anti-di.description: An anti-discrimination policy can be an important tool for creating a fair and inclusive workplace or community.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/absence.title: Absence
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/absence.description: Absence refers to the state or fact of being away from a place or not present at a particular time.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/annual-.title: Annual Leave Loading
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/annual-.description: Annual leave loading is extra pay given during annual leave to compensate employees for wages they would earn if they were working.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/annual-.title: Annual Leave Entitlements
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/annual-.description: Annual leave entitlements are the amount of vacation time or time off that an employee is entitled to receive with pay.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/base-pa.title: Base Pay
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/base-pa.description: Base pay is the fixed amount of money that an employee is paid for their work, not including any additional pay for overtime, bonuses, or other forms of compensation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/abscond.title: Absconding
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/abscond.description: Absconding is the act of leaving a job or place of work without permission or notice. It can disrupt operations and lead to disciplinary action by the employer.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/annual-.title: Annual Leave
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/annual-.description: Annual leave is typically accrued over time, meaning that an employee earns a certain amount each year based on the number of hours worked or the length of employment.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/ban-the.title: Ban the Box
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/ban-the.description: Ban the Box is a policy that prohibits employers from asking about criminal history on job applications and in initial job interviews.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/abilene.title: Abilene Paradox
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/abilene.description: The Abilene Paradox is the phenomenon of a group making a decision that is counter to the individual preferences of its members.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/abandon.title: Abandonment Rates
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/abandon.description: Abandonment rates refer to the percentage of people who do not complete a desired action, such as making a purchase or filling out a form.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/balance.title: Balanced Scorecard
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/balance.description: A balanced scorecard is a strategic performance measurement system that helps organizations to track and monitor their performance across four different perspectives: financial, customer, internal process, and learning and growth.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/america.title: Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/america.description: The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) is a federal law that prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities in employment and transportation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/backgro.title: Background Verification
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/backgro.description: Background verification is the process of verifying and checking the accuracy of information provided by an individual.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/ambiver.title: Ambivert
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/ambiver.description: Ambiverts are people who exhibit characteristics of both introverts and extroverts. They are somewhere in between the two and have a balance of introverted and extroverted qualities.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/backgro.title: Background Screening
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/backgro.description: Background screening verifies identity, work history, education, and more to ensure candidate suitability, protect employers, and support safe hiring decisions.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/alterna.title: Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR)
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/alterna.description: Alternate Dispute Resolution (ADR) refers to a variety of methods for resolving disputes outside of the traditional judicial system, such as arbitration, mediation, and negotiation.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/back-pa.title: Back Pay
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/back-pa.description: Back pay is a type of payment that is made to an employee to compensate them for wages that they should have been paid in the past but were not. This can occur for a variety of reasons, such as an error in payroll, a violation of the employee’s contract or employment law, or a period of time when the employee was not paid due to a dispute with their employer.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-rel.title: Job Relatedness
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-rel.description: Job Relatedness refers to the extent to which a particular job or task is relevant to or related to an organization’s overall goals and objectives.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/first-i.title: First Impression Error
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/first-i.description: First Impression Error, also known as the “Halo Effect,” refers to the tendency for an initial positive or negative impression of a person to influence subsequent judgments or evaluations.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/constru.title: Construct Validity
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/constru.description: Construct Validity is the extent to which a measure or test accurately reflects the concept or construct it is intended to measure.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/agile-o.title: Agile Organizations
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/agile-o.description: An Agile organization is one that values flexibility and adaptability in its processes and decision-making.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compres.title: Compressed Work Week
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/compres.description: A Compressed Work Week is a type of work schedule in which employees work a full-time schedule in fewer than the traditional five workdays per week.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/temp-to.title: Temp-to-Hire
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/temp-to.description: Temp-to-Hire, also known as Temporary-to-Permanent, is an employment arrangement in which an employee is initially hired temporarily, with the possibility of being offered a permanent position after a certain period.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/conting.title: Contingency Recruitment
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/conting.description: Contingency Recruitment is a type of recruitment in which a company hires an agency only if they successfully fill the open positions, based on a fee.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/benchma.title: Benchmark Job
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/benchma.description: A benchmark job is a role with standardised duties, common across the labour market, and well-represented in salary surveys, used as an anchor point in compensation benchmarking. What makes a job a benchmark job Not every role qualifies as a benchmark job. A benchmark job must satisfy most of the following criteria – typically five…

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/open-in.title: Open Interview
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/open-in.description: An Open Interview, lets candidates attend without an appointment, ideal for quickly filling multiple positions or screening many candidates.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/group-i.title: Group Interview
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/group-i.description: A Group Interview is a method of interviewing where multiple candidates are interviewed simultaneously by a group of interviewers, typically to assess social and teamworking skills.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/time-in.title: Time in Lieu
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/time-in.description: Time-in-Lieu (also known as “Compensatory Time Off”) is a benefit that allows employees to take time off from work in exchange for working additional hours or overtime.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labour-.title: Labour Turnover
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/labour-.description: Labour turnover refers to the rate at which employees leave an organization and are replaced.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/exit-in.title: Exit Interview
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/exit-in.description: An Exit Interview is a conversation with a departing employee to gather their feedback and insights on the company, job, and reasons for leaving.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/rightsi.title: Rightsizing
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/rightsi.description: Rightsizing is the process of adjusting the size of a company or organization to better align with its needs and goals.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/backfil.title: Backfill Position
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/backfil.description: Backfill position refers to a job that is temporarily or permanently filled by another employee after the original employee leaves or is promoted.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/agile-h.title: Agile HR
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/agile-h.description: Agile HR is a modern approach to managing HR functions, emphasizing flexibility, speed, and collaboration.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/floatin.title: Floating Holiday
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/floatin.description: A Floating Holiday is paid time off granted to employees in addition to their regular vacation, sick, and personal days.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bereave.title: Bereavement Leave
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/bereave.description: Bereavement leave is time off from work that is granted to employees following the death of a close family member.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/diversi.title: Diversity Candidate
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/diversi.description: Diversity Candidate hiring is actively seeking and considering candidates from diverse backgrounds and experiences for job openings within an organization.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/assessm.title: Assessment Centre
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/assessm.description: An Assessment Centre is a structured and systematic method of evaluating the potential of job candidates or employees for a particular role or development opportunity.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employm.title: Employment Agency
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/employm.description: An Employment Agency is a company that helps job seekers find employment and helps employers find qualified candidates for job openings.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-req.title: Job Requisition
https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-req.description: A Job Requisition is a formal request for a new or additional employee to be hired within an organization, and job Requisitions are typically used to initiate the recruitment process.

https://testlify.com/hr-glossary/job-boa.title: Job Board
